items.title: 中國反制！擬管制40類技術出口
items.title_en: China Countermeasures! Plans to Regulate Export of 40 Types of Technology
paras: 中國商務部與科技部近日聯合提出一項出口管制新規，擬對人工智慧、半導體、生物醫藥和太陽能等領域的40類技術實施出口限制或禁止。
該提案於10月16日公布，目前正面向社會公開徵求意見，截止日期為2026年11月15日。根據文件內容，14類技術可能被禁止出口，26類技術將面臨不同程度的限制。
在人工智慧領域，提案涵蓋23個技術方向，具體管制措施包括：禁止出口利用AI生成和修改惡意代碼的技術，限制特定AI晶片和存儲電路設計技術，以及限制參數規模達到2兆及以上或具備特定先進能力的大模型出口。
此外，涉及敏感國家數據的AI技術境外轉移也可能被禁止。
不過，該措施並不意味著中國AI模型的境外訪問被完全切斷。中國商務部說，通過API接口、應用程式、網站和SaaS服務等方式使用受限模型，不被視為技術本身的出口。已公開發布於開源社區或學術論文中的解決方案，擬不受出口管制約束。
在半導體和太陽能領域，提案擬對多晶矽、矽片和太陽能電池的生產技術實施限制。生物醫藥方面，部分細胞與基因治療平台技術可能被禁止出口。
中國有關部門表示，此舉旨在維護國家安全，防止敏感技術不受控制擴散。在新版目錄正式生效前，出口經營者須登記受臨時措施管轄的技術轉移。
此次提案正值美中科技博弈持續升溫之際。今年7月，美國曾以保護關鍵AI基礎設施免受網路間諜和破壞風險為由，禁止進口中國製造的機器人和電力逆變器。
分析人士指出，中國此次擬議的出口管制清單，是在全球技術競爭加劇背景下，對自身關鍵技術優勢進行系統性保護的舉措。
paras_en: China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology recently jointly proposed a new export control regulation, aiming to impose export restrictions or bans on 40 categories of technology in fields such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors, biomedicine and solar energy.

The proposal was announced on October 16 and is currently open for public comment, with the deadline set for November 15, 2026. According to the document, 14 categories of technology could be prohibited from export, while 26 categories would face varying degrees of restriction.

In the AI sector, the proposal covers 23 technology directions. Specific control measures include banning the export of technologies that use AI to generate or modify malicious code, restricting certain AI chips and memory circuit design technologies, and limiting the export of large models with parameter scales of 2 trillion or more or possessing specific advanced capabilities.
In addition, the overseas transfer of AI technologies involving sensitive national data may also be prohibited.

However, the measure does not mean that overseas access to Chinese AI models will be completely cut off. The Ministry of Commerce said that using restricted models via API interfaces, applications, websites and SaaS services is not considered an export of the technology itself. Solutions that have been publicly released in open‑source communities or academic papers are intended to be exempt from export controls.

In the semiconductor and solar sectors, the proposal seeks to restrict production technologies for polysilicon, silicon wafers and solar cells. In biomedicine, certain cell and gene therapy platform technologies may be banned from export.

Chinese authorities said the move aims to safeguard national security and prevent uncontrolled diffusion of sensitive technologies. Until the new catalogue formally takes effect, exporters must register technology transfers that fall under the temporary measures.

The proposal comes as the US‑China technology rivalry continues to heat up. In July this year, the United States banned imports of Chinese‑made robots and power inverters, citing the need to protect critical AI infrastructure from cyber espionage and sabotage risks.
Analysts note that China's proposed export control list is a systematic effort to protect its own key technology advantages amid intensifying global tech competition.

items.title_en: Opening in Hell? Nasdaq Futures Down 8 Days Straight, Taiwan Stocks Plunge a Thousand Points? Retail Investors Survival: Don’t Miss These Two Steps!
paras: 費半連續8個交易日收黑，創2008年以來最長的連跌紀錄，指數大跌11.4%。外資也沒閒著，連8日賣超，累計超過6,800億元下。今日台股恐怕將出現「千點海嘯」。但這波全球股市回檔，江江要問你一件重要的事：「公司是賺不到錢了，還是大家把價格砍得比較狠？」
其實這波賣壓來自三個擔心：
一、AI投資什麼時候回本
二、企業舉債擴張
三、油價大漲à升息
這些都是「估值」的問題，也就是市場願意為未來付多少錢。它們不是「訂單消失了」的問題。這就好像：你家附近的海鮮攤，今天魚沒壞、冷凍櫃沒停電，只是新聞說「海鮮價格可能太貴」，客人嚇得全跑了。老闆被迫降價清貨，但魚還是那些魚。這就是台股正在發生的事！
如果今天是基本面崩壞，你應該會看到雲端四大巨頭砍資本支出、台積電(2330-TW)接單被取消、輝達(NVDA-US)晶片賣不出去。但現實情況是什麼？
一、台積電 剛公佈的第3季獲利年增高達 69%，魏哲家明確表示先進製程「需求遠大於供給」。
二、輝達 執行長黃仁勳也站出來定心丸，強調 AI 帶來的生產力革命才剛開始。
三、美國四大雲端巨頭（CSP）明年的資本支出更是持續上修、甚至成長六成突破 1.5 兆美元。
數據明明白白擺在眼前：AI 的實質需求與獲利爆發力完全沒變。市場現在殺的，純粹是之前漲太快、基期太高、融資開太滿的高槓桿籌碼。主力藉著外資大賣與短期利空，順水推舟來一場「大甩轎」，把不堅定的散戶清洗出場！
面對千點海嘯，請緊記這兩大保命心法
一、不盲目殺低。 恐慌時砍掉的，常常是下個月業績最好的那幾檔。先看個股基本面和技術面，不要讓情緒下單。
二、不急著抄底。分批布局遠比一次押滿更重要
！行情要落底，技術面上必須等待 急跌盤底、出現向上跳空缺口，以及 MACD 柱狀體出現收腳。等訊號確立後再進場，你的資金安全度和勝率會高出許多。

paras_en: The Nasdaq futures have posted eight consecutive losing days, the longest streak since 2008, with the index dropping 11.4%. Foreign investors are also active, selling for eight straight days and netting over NT$680 billion. Today Taiwan’s market may see a “thousand‑point tsunami”. Yet this global market pull‑back raises a key question: “Is it that companies can’t make money, or are investors simply cutting prices harder?”
In fact, this selling pressure stems from three concerns:
1. When will AI investments break even?
2. Corporate debt‑financed expansion
3. Surge in oil prices leading to rate hikes

These are all valuation issues – how much the market is willing to pay for future earnings – not a “vanishing order” problem. It’s like a seafood stall near your home: the fish are fresh, the freezers are fine, but a news story says “seafood may be too pricey,” scaring customers away. The owner must slash prices, yet the fish remain the same. That’s what’s happening to Taiwan’s market!
If fundamentals were collapsing, you’d see the four cloud giants cutting capex, TSMC (2330‑TW) losing orders, and Nvidia (NVDA‑US) chips not selling. But what’s the reality?
1. TSMC just reported Q3 earnings up 69% year‑over‑year, and CEO Wei‑Zhe‑Jia clearly said demand for advanced processes “far exceeds supply.”
2. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang also stepped in to reassure, emphasizing that the productivity revolution driven by AI is only just beginning.
3. The four U.S. cloud service providers are raising next year’s capex, even boosting it by 60% to exceed $1.5 trillion.

The data are plain: real AI demand and profit‑driving power haven’t changed. What the market is killing now are the high‑leverage positions that rode a too‑fast rally, a high base and over‑extended financing. Main players, using foreign‑investor selling and short‑term negatives, are staging a “big dump” to wash out weak retail investors!
Facing a thousand‑point tsunami, remember these two survival principles:
1. Don’t blindly chase low‑price stocks. In panic, you often cut the stocks that will post the best earnings next month. Check fundamentals and technicals first; don’t let emotion drive your orders.
2. Don’t rush to bottom‑fish. Staggered positioning is far more important than loading up in one go.

When the market bottoms, you must wait for technical signs: a sharp‑drop bottom, an upward gap, and MACD histogram turning up. Enter only after those signals confirm – your capital safety and win rate will be much higher.
Big players are quietly building positions! Pull‑back locks in these six “excellent‑chip” indicator stocks

When the market is most fearful, it’s the moment for “early‑bird” investors. While retail investors flee, foreign investors, mutual funds and large accounts are already locking in low‑base, high‑growth quality stocks. Below are six well‑positioned indicator stocks worth adding to your watchlist during the pull‑back:
Foreign‑investor lock‑in indicators:

1. Guoguang (6209‑TW): Successfully pivoted to automotive lenses and IoT optics, dramatically improving its product mix. With rising automotive lens shipments and a higher share of high‑margin products, profit structure has strengthened, prompting foreign investors to snap up positions.

2. TaiBiaoTech (6278‑TW): Global leader in SMT assembly, deep‑focused on AI server boards and automotive electronics. Benefiting from strong demand for high‑end boards and expanding low‑earth‑orbit satellite applications, it maintains rapid growth, earning double‑lock‑in from foreign investors and large accounts.
Mutual‑fund lock‑in indicators:

3. Jinxiang Electronics (2368‑TW): Absolute leader in high‑layer AI server PCBs. With massive shipments of 800 Gbps switches and next‑gen AI server boards, average selling price and gross margin keep rising, fueling profit momentum and strong mutual‑fund positioning.

4. Daliu (3167‑TW): High‑end PCB and semiconductor packaging equipment maker, venturing into CoWoS advanced packaging. Riding urgent orders from major semiconductor firms expanding capacity, order visibility is extremely high, and revenue and profit are exploding multiplicatively.
Large‑account lock‑in indicators:

5. Fanquan (6830‑TW): Leader in semiconductor material analysis, a key component for silicon‑photonics CPO and advanced‑process R&D. Benefiting from booming demand for advanced‑process inspection, quarterly revenue hits new highs, attracting large accounts to add on the dip.

6. Zhongda‑KY (4977‑TW): Leading high‑speed optical transceiver module maker, deep in CPO (co‑packaged optics) technology. Driven by AI compute centers’ urgent need for high‑bandwidth transmission, new‑generation product mass‑production brings huge profit‑growth flexibility.
Conclusion: The end of a crash often marks the start of huge profits!

There’s a market adage: “Only those who dare to see opportunity in a crash earn the ensuing gains.” Market sentiment is as changeable as weather, but industry long‑term trends are like the seasons – inevitable. When a plunge pushes quality stocks back near their long‑term averages, it becomes the best gift for rational investors.

Reminder: Don’t let emotion make decisions! Preserve capital, stay calm, and stagger purchases of low‑base, strong‑chip stocks. When a gap appears and sentiment warms, you’ll thank your cool, wise self!

items.title: 烏克蘭命運由三強決定？普丁邀川普、習近平談停戰 排除澤倫斯基
items.title_en: Ukraine's Fate Decided by Three Powers? Putin Invites Trump and Xi to Discuss Ceasefire, Excluding Zelensky
paras: 《華爾街日報》引述消息人士報導，俄羅斯總統普丁提議，下月與美國總統川普及中國國家主席習近平會面，討論烏克蘭問題，試圖協商出有利於莫斯科的方案，結束這場延續四年的戰爭。
這項提議顯示，普丁正試圖趁美俄領袖關係回暖之際推進自身目標，兩人關係升溫已讓烏克蘭及其在華府和歐洲的盟友感到不安。
若在烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基未參與的情況下舉行這類峰會，將是前所未見的安排，也將讓歐洲各國乃至其他地區拉響警報。
一名聽取相關簡報的俄羅斯前情報官員表示，普丁在10月9日與川普通話時提出這項構想。雙方也在那次通話中達成協議，由美國購買俄羅斯柴油，並協助其銷往全球市場。
克里姆林宮發言人佩斯科夫證實，各方正就可能舉行的會議進行討論。
他向《華爾街日報》表示：「目前對於會議本身或可能的議程，都還沒有明確共識，不過三方均承認，理論上有可能舉行這樣的會議。」
一名美國高階官員表示，川普尚未同意出席這類峰會。不過，考量到川普希望兌現結束戰爭的競選承諾，他可能願意接受這項構想。
川普曾宣稱，會在新任期的「第一天」結束戰爭，如今他上任卻已將近兩年。
消息人士指出，克里姆林宮建議，在即將登場的亞太經濟合作會議（APEC）峰會期間，另行舉行三方對話。這場峰會將於11月18日至19日在中國南方科技重鎮深圳舉行。
研究中國的分析人士表示，若三方對話在中國舉行，將是習近平提升中國外交斡旋地位的一大進展。其他熟悉近期俄中磋商的人士透露，俄方官員已透過外交管道向北京提出構想，中方則表示，只要川普同意，就不會反對。
華府智庫史汀生中心中國計畫主任孫韻表示：「中國希望被視為大國之間的樞紐，也可能成為美俄之間的調停者。」
白宮不予置評，中國駐美大使館也未回應置評請求。
上述俄羅斯前情報官員表示，普丁過去也曾向川普和習近平提議舉行三方峰會，但這次提議的背景，是莫斯科與華府的關係出現轉機。
川普剛與普丁達成購買俄羅斯柴油的協議，希望藉此壓低燃料價格。高油價已拖累美國經濟，也衝擊共和黨在期中選舉前的選情。
上周五，川普暫停執行他上月簽署的一項跨黨派法案所規定的對俄制裁，引發國會議員批評，其中包括部分盟友。白宮高階官員表示，川普是在認為幾乎沒有其他有效降價選項後，才做出這些決定。
能源專家普遍認為，伊朗戰爭才是柴油價格上漲的主因，而俄羅斯承諾出售的燃料數量，不足以對市場產生太大影響。
與此同時，川普再度表達對澤倫斯基的不滿，要求烏克蘭停止攻擊俄羅斯煉油廠，並暗示烏克蘭需要一位新總統。美國主導的停戰斡旋則大致陷入停滯。
烏克蘭周日稍早攻擊普丁家鄉聖彼得堡的一座石油碼頭後，川普隨即在Truth Social發文抨擊澤倫斯基。
他指控這位烏克蘭領袖鎖定俄羅斯柴油煉製設施發動攻擊，並稱澤倫斯基「不想結束這場戰爭，而且可能從來就不想」。
川普表示，他暫緩實施制裁，是因為不想讓俄羅斯退出談判。他寫道：「我要這場戰爭結束。」
莫斯科將可能舉行的三方對話，視為鞏固俄羅斯全球強權地位的途徑。這也是普丁自2000年入主克里姆林宮以來，一直追求的地位。
這種會議形式也將歐洲排除在外，而克里姆林宮認為，歐洲是俄羅斯在烏克蘭取得勝利的主要障礙。
俄羅斯前情報官員表示，普丁對三方會談抱持宏大、卻不切實際的企圖，希望將其打造為第二次雅爾達峰會，藉此劃分全球勢力範圍。
即使習近平和川普不太可能同意這種安排，美、俄、中三國領袖共同談判另一個國家命運的畫面，仍將釋出強烈訊號。
不過，這場峰會對習近平而言也並非毫無風險。部分熟悉討論的人士表示，中國官員擔心，這場地緣政治插曲可能喧賓奪主，掩蓋北京原本希望透過APEC展現中國區域角色的安排。
上述人士指出，習近平正試圖在持續支持普丁與維繫中國對歐經濟關係之間，小心拿捏平衡。這類三方會談可能讓中國更直接捲入烏克蘭戰爭，也可能引發歐洲各國反彈；歐洲原本就對北京偏向莫斯科的立場抱持戒心。
paras_en: The Wall Street Journal, citing sources, reports that Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed meeting next month with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss the Ukraine issue, seeking a Moscow-favorable solution to end the four-year war.
The proposal shows Putin is trying to push his agenda while U.S.-Russia relations warm, a development that has made Ukraine and its allies in Washington and Europe uneasy.
Holding such a summit without Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky would be unprecedented and would set off alarms across Europe and elsewhere.

A former Russian intelligence officer who briefed on the matter said Putin raised the idea during a Mandarin‑language call with Trump on Oct. 9, and the two also agreed that the U.S. would purchase Russian diesel and help ship it worldwide.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed that the parties are discussing a possible meeting.
He told the Wall Street Journal, "There is no clear consensus yet on the meeting itself or its agenda, but all three sides acknowledge that, in theory, such a meeting could take place."
A senior U.S. official said Trump has not yet agreed to attend such a summit, but given his desire to fulfill a campaign promise to end the war, he might be willing to consider it.
Trump has claimed he will end the war on the "first day" of his new term, yet he is now approaching two years into his presidency.
Sources say the Kremlin suggested holding a three‑way dialogue during the upcoming APEC summit, which will be held Nov. 18‑19 in Shenzhen, China’s high‑tech hub in the south.

China analysts note that a trilateral dialogue in China would boost Xi’s diplomatic stature, and insiders familiar with recent Russia‑China talks say Russian officials have floated the idea through diplomatic channels, with Beijing saying it would not object if Trump agrees.
Sun Yun, director of the China program at the Stimson Center, said, "China wants to be seen as a hub among great powers and could even become a mediator between the U.S. and Russia."
The White House declined to comment, and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment.
The former intelligence officer added that Putin had previously suggested a three‑way summit to Trump and Xi, but this time the backdrop is a turning point in U.S.–Russia relations.
Trump recently struck a diesel‑purchase deal with Putin, hoping to lower fuel prices; high oil prices have weighed on the U.S. economy and hurt Republican prospects ahead of the midterms.

Last Friday, Trump paused enforcement of a bipartisan sanctions law against Russia that he signed last month, drawing criticism from members of Congress, including some allies. A senior White House official said Trump acted only after concluding there were few other effective ways to cut prices.
Energy experts generally attribute the diesel price surge to the Iran war, noting that the volume Russia has pledged to sell is too small to move the market significantly.

At the same time, Trump reiterated his displeasure with Zelensky, demanding Ukraine stop attacks on Russian refineries and hinting Ukraine needs a new president. U.S.-led cease‑fire mediation has largely stalled.
After Ukraine struck a Russian oil terminal in St. Petersburg earlier on Sunday, Trump immediately posted on Truth Social criticizing Zelensky.
He accused the Ukrainian leader of targeting Russian diesel‑refining facilities and said Zelensky "doesn't want to end the war and may never have wanted to."
Trump said he delayed sanctions because he didn't want Russia to walk away from negotiations, writing, "I want this war to end."
Moscow sees a possible three‑way dialogue as a way to cement Russia’s global great‑power status, a goal Putin has pursued since taking the Kremlin in 2000.
Such a format would also sideline Europe, which the Kremlin views as the main obstacle to a Russian victory in Ukraine.
The former intelligence officer said Putin’s grand but unrealistic vision for a trilateral talk aims to create a second Yalta, carving up global spheres of influence.
Even if Xi and Trump are unlikely to agree to the arrangement, the image of the U.S., Russia and China jointly negotiating another country's fate would send a strong signal.
However, the summit also carries risks for Xi. Some insiders say Chinese officials worry the geopolitical side‑show could eclipse Beijing’s plan to use APEC to showcase its regional role.

Those sources note Xi is trying to balance continued support for Putin with maintaining China’s economic ties to Europe, and a three‑way talk could pull China deeper into the Ukraine war and provoke European backlash, as Europe already views Beijing’s tilt toward Moscow with suspicion.

items.title: 美烏矛盾與法國騷亂推升美元！歐元兌多數G10貨幣走貶 今早兌美元一度大跌0.5%
items.title_en: US-Ukraine Tensions and French Unrest Boost the Dollar! Euro Falls Against Most G10 Currencies, Briefly Dropping 0.5% Against the Dollar This Morning
paras: 受美烏矛盾進一步升高及法國大規模抗議活動影響，市場對歐元信心受挫，歐元兌多數G10貨幣在今(19)日亞洲早盤交易時段走低。
周末期間，法國多個城市抗議活動演變為警方與示威者之間的衝突，爆發法國多年來最嚴重的街頭暴力事件，出現搶劫、地標建築遭縱火情況。歐洲多國接連發生示威活動，法國的抗議規模最大，比利時、義大利、葡萄牙也受到波及。與此同時，烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基周日(18日)指責川普試圖向基輔施壓，逼迫烏克蘭向俄羅斯投降。
歐元兌美元在今日早盤一度貶值0.5%，最低貶至 1.1183 美元，隨後部分收復跌幅，交投於 1.1212 美元附近。受歐元走弱拖累，東歐貨幣表現弱於其他新興市場貨幣，美元兌波蘭茲羅提升值0.5%，報3.9071；美元兌匈牙利福林走升0.5%，報324.88，美元兌保加利亞列弗亦升值0.5%，報1.7485。
澳洲聯邦銀行外匯策略師Carol Kong表示：「市場恐將持續為歐元計入風險溢價。歐元兌美元本周可能測試 1.1130支撐價位，尤其是在地緣緊張進一步推高美元的情況下。」
paras_en: Rising US‑Ukraine tensions and large‑scale protests in France have dented market confidence in the euro, causing the euro to fall against most G10 currencies during Asian early‑trade on the 19th.

Over the weekend, protests in several French cities escalated into clashes between police and demonstrators, sparking the most severe street violence France has seen in years, including robberies and arson of landmark buildings. Demonstrations spread across multiple European countries, with France seeing the largest protests, and Belgium, Italy and Portugal also affected. At the same time, Ukrainian President Zelensky on Sunday (the 18th) accused former U.S. President Trump of trying to pressure Kyiv into surrendering to Russia.

The euro‑dollar pair slipped as much as 0.5% in early trade today, hitting a low of 1.1183 USD before partially regaining ground and trading around 1.1212 USD. The euro’s weakness also weighed on Eastern European currencies, which underperformed other emerging‑market currencies: the dollar rose 0.5% against the Polish zloty to 3.9071, against the Hungarian forint to 324.88, and against the Bulgarian lev to 1.7485.

Carol Kong, FX strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said: “The market is likely to continue pricing a risk premium into the euro. The euro‑dollar pair could test the 1.1130 support level this week, especially if geopolitical tensions further lift the dollar.”

items.title: 外資撤走逾千億億美元 韓股從AI贏家變重災區、散戶慘套
items.title_en: Foreign Investors Pull Out Over $100 Billion; Korean Stocks Shift from AI Winners to Disaster Zone, Retail Investors Suffer
paras: 韓國股市從AI行情的大贏家，轉為外資大舉撤出的重災區。南韓綜合指數(KOSPI) ）上半年一度漲逾一倍，下半年至今卻下跌40%，成交額較5月底高峰萎縮逾七成。隨著外資賣股、企業回購接近尾聲，追逐AI熱潮進場的投資人，正承受資金退潮的衝擊。
韓國確實受惠於AI產業蓬勃發展。三星電子(005930KS) 與SK海力士(000660KS) 位居記憶體、HBM及AI伺服器供應鏈核心，營收與獲利成長帶來實質經濟貢獻，估值又低於美國科技巨頭，成為全球資金布局AI的重要標的。
AI紅利推升股價 外資轉身撤離
在投行研究報告、ETF資金與衍生性商品槓桿推動下，記憶體股逐漸從傳統景氣循環股，被市場視為AI基礎設施成長股，帶動KOSPI上半年領漲全球主要股市。
然而，當估值與獲利預期持續攀升，企業繳出亮眼成績，也未必足以推動股價。前期積極買進的外資轉向獲利了結，曾經推升行情的資金，成為下半年賣壓的重要來源。
即使歷經修正，KOSPI自2025年以來累計漲幅仍超過130%。三星與SK海力士股價雖從高檔回落約一半，過去兩年市值漲幅仍分別超過三倍及6.4倍，凸顯不同進場時點的投資人，面臨截然不同的結果。
外資賣超集中兩大龍頭
截至10月14日，外資今年在韓國主要股票市場累計淨賣出約203.7兆韓元，其中三星與SK海力士合計約176兆韓元，占總賣超約86%。今年外資從韓國股市撤出約1,310億美元，規模居亞洲主要市場之首。
韓國對外資的依賴，也反映在持股結構。截至今年6月，外資持有韓股總市值比重約37.8%至38.9%，美國投資人約占外資持股的42%。
三星外資持股比率從8月初約46.70%，降至10月初的46.38%，為2008年以來最低；SK海力士則從50.84%降至49.59%，低於十年平均。
兩家公司合計占KOSPI權重超過一半，外資集中出售這兩檔股票，對指數形成明顯壓力。10月14日，韓國國民年金基金在國會聽證會上，甚至被批評是「外國投資者的提款機」，反映市場對外資撤離與本土資金承接賣壓的不滿。
回購將退場 散戶承接力轉弱
韓股面臨的另一項問題，是外資持續賣出之際，其他買盤也逐漸減弱。
7月股市重挫後，散戶進場意願降溫。融資餘額從6月高峰38.6兆韓元降至約33兆韓元，券商帳戶待投資存款也從接近140兆韓元，減少至約100兆韓元，顯示市場可動用資金縮水。
先前支撐行情的企業回購，同樣接近尾聲。三星與SK海力士合計約55兆韓元的回購計畫，貢獻了上月市場大部分買盤，但三星回購已於10月上旬基本完成，SK海力士也僅剩少量收尾。
當外資賣壓延續、回購逐步退場，散戶又縮減投入，市場便缺乏足夠承接力量。企業仍具產業優勢，並不代表股價能免於資金撤離的衝擊。
產業仍有優勢 市場結構卻脆弱
這波修正並不代表韓國AI半導體產業失去競爭力，而是暴露股市過度集中的風險。當指數高度依賴兩家公司、單一產業與外部資金，漲勢容易被放大，資金撤離時也缺少緩衝。
1997年亞洲金融危機期間，韓國財閥高負債擴張，金融體系依賴海外資金續借，國際資本撤出後，韓元與股市重挫，最終被迫接受國際貨幣基金（IMF）援助。
這次情況與當年不同，風險主要集中於市場結構：外資對核心股票價格具有高度影響力，散戶透過槓桿與ETF參與，企業回購則成為短期支撐。一旦資金流向改變，這些支撐便可能同步轉弱。
不過，將跌勢全數歸咎於外資，也忽略了資金配置的現實。下半年貨幣政策預期由寬鬆轉向緊縮，升息與無風險收益率走高，都促使投資人重新比較不同市場的報酬與估值，獲利了結也有其背景。
槓桿放大跌幅 高檔進場代價沉重
對高檔進場的投資人而言，槓桿進一步放大損失。在香港掛牌、曾受到追捧的兩倍做多SK海力士ETF，最新報價為19.22元，相較6月底高點193.65元，跌幅約91%。
韓股這輪大起大落顯示，產業成長與投資報酬並非必然同步。AI帶來的營收與獲利紅利仍在，但股價還取決於估值、資金流向與市場承接能力。
當外資撤離、回購減弱，最晚進場且使用高槓桿的投資人，往往承受最沉重的修正代價。
paras_en: Korean equities have shifted from being the big winners of the AI rally to a disaster zone as foreign investors pull out en masse. The KOSPI index, which surged more than double in the first half of the year, has fallen about 40% in the second half and trading volume has shrunk by over 70% from its late‑May peak. As foreign selling and corporate buybacks near their end, investors who chased the AI hype are now feeling the impact of a capital outflow.

South Korea has indeed benefited from the booming AI industry. Samsung Electronics (005930KS) and SK Hynix (000660KS) sit at the core of the memory, HBM and AI‑server supply chain, delivering real economic contribution through revenue and profit growth, and their valuations remain lower than those of U.S. tech giants, making them key targets for global AI capital allocation.
AI‑driven upside lifts stock prices, foreign investors turn away

Backed by investment‑bank research reports, ETF inflows and leveraged derivative products, memory stocks have gradually been re‑classified from traditional cyclical plays to AI‑infrastructure growth stocks, helping the KOSPI lead global major markets in the first half of the year.

However, as valuations and profit expectations kept climbing, even stellar corporate results were not enough to sustain price gains. Foreign investors who bought aggressively early are now taking profits, and the capital that once propelled the rally has become a major source of selling pressure in the second half.

Even after the correction, the KOSPI has risen more than 130% since 2025. Although Samsung and SK Hynix have each fallen roughly half from their peaks, their market caps have still more than tripled and increased 6.4‑fold respectively over the past two years, highlighting how investors who entered at different times face vastly different outcomes.
Foreign investors’ net selling is concentrated in two giants

As of Oct. 14, foreign investors have sold a net total of about KRW 203.7 trillion in Korea’s main equity market this year, with Samsung and SK Hynix accounting for roughly KRW 176 trillion, or about 86% of the total outflow. Foreign investors have withdrawn roughly $131 billion from Korean stocks this year, the largest pull‑back among Asian markets.

Korea’s reliance on foreign capital is also reflected in its ownership structure. By June this year, foreign investors held about 37.8%‑38.9% of the total market value of Korean equities, with U.S. investors accounting for roughly 42% of foreign holdings.
Foreign ownership of Samsung fell from about 46.70% in early August to 46.38% in early October, the lowest level since 2008; SK Hynix’s fell from 50.84% to 49.59%, below its ten‑year average.

The two companies together make up more than half of the KOSPI’s weighting, so foreign investors’ concentrated selling of these stocks puts clear pressure on the index. On Oct. 14, the Korean National Pension Service was even criticized in a parliamentary hearing as a “cash‑cow for foreign investors,” reflecting market frustration over foreign exits and domestic capital’s limited ability to absorb the selling.
Buybacks are winding down and retail buying power is weakening
Another issue for Korean stocks is that as foreign investors keep selling, other buying pressure is also fading.

After the market plunge in July, retail enthusiasm cooled. Margin balances fell from a June peak of KRW 38.6 trillion to about KRW 33 trillion, and broker‑account cash earmarked for investment dropped from nearly KRW 140 trillion to roughly KRW 100 trillion, indicating a shrinkage in deployable capital.

Corporate buybacks that had previously supported the rally are also nearing completion. Samsung and SK Hynix together have a KRW 55 trillion buyback program that supplied most of last month’s buying, but Samsung’s repurchase was essentially finished in early October and SK Hynix has only a small tail left.

When foreign selling persists, buybacks retreat, and retail investors cut back, the market lacks sufficient support. The companies still have industry advantages, but that does not shield their share prices from the impact of capital outflows.
Industry strengths remain but market structure is fragile

This correction does not mean Korea’s AI semiconductor sector has lost its competitiveness; rather, it exposes the risk of an overly concentrated market. When an index is heavily dependent on two firms, a single industry and foreign capital, gains can be amplified and withdrawals leave little buffer.

During the 1997 Asian financial crisis, Korean chaebols expanded with high debt and the financial system relied on overseas funding. When international capital fled, the won and the stock market crashed, eventually forcing Korea to accept IMF assistance.

The current situation differs from 1997; the risk now lies mainly in market structure: foreign investors wield outsized influence over core stock prices, retail investors participate via leverage and ETFs, and corporate buybacks act as short‑term support. If capital flows shift, those supports can weaken simultaneously.

Nevertheless, blaming the entire decline on foreign investors ignores the realities of fund allocation. In the second half of the year, monetary policy expectations are shifting from easing to tightening, with higher rates and risk‑free yields prompting investors to reassess returns and valuations across markets, making profit‑taking understandable.
Leverage magnifies losses; buying at highs is costly

For investors who entered at lofty levels, leverage further amplifies losses. The SK Hynix double‑long ETF listed in Hong Kong, once hotly chased, now trades at 19.22 HKD, down from its late‑June high of 193.65 HKD – a drop of about 91%.

This roller‑coaster in Korean stocks shows that industry growth and investment returns do not automatically move together. AI‑driven revenue and profit upside remain, but share prices still depend on valuations, capital flows and market‑absorption capacity.
When foreign investors exit and buybacks weaken, the latest entrants who used high leverage tend to bear the heaviest correction costs.

items.title: 美烏矛盾持續升級！澤倫斯基控美施壓「投降」後提新條件：停打俄煉油廠換「愛國者」飛彈
items.title_en: US‑Ukraine Rift Escalates: Zelensky Accuses Washington of Pressuring Ukraine to ‘Surrender’ and Offers New Terms – Halt Attacks on Russian Refineries in Exchange for Patriot Missiles
paras: 烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基週日(18日)接受《彭博資訊》訪問時指控，美國正透過軍援、衛星通信與能源政策向基輔施壓，試圖迫使烏國接受對俄有利的停戰條件，但他也強調並非斷言華府以此為目標，但近期一連串動作「看起來如此」，雙方持續一週的公開爭執進一步升級。
爭議核心從烏軍打擊俄國煉油廠，外溢至對俄制裁、星鏈與軍用星盾服務、情資共享及愛國者飛彈供應。澤倫斯基提出交換方案：烏方停止攻擊俄柴油供應鏈，美國則增供愛國者攔截彈保護能源設施與城市，但華府目前僅要求烏國停手，未接受交換。
華府立場為壓低能源價格、維持與莫斯科談判渠道，稱與俄柴油供應安排是避免「把普丁趕出談判桌」，並反指澤倫斯基拖延戰事。
基輔的立場則認為，俄軍持續轟炸烏國能源設施之際，華府卻減輕俄經濟壓力，只會削弱逼俄收手動能。
星鏈與情資爭議加劇。澤倫斯基稱烏國境內設備時速逾161公里後服務受限，矛頭指向白宮，華府否認下達指令。此外，澤倫斯基證實美一度暫停預警俄彈道飛彈來襲的共享機制，之後恢復。
與此同時，愛國者交付也成摩擦點：澤倫斯基說烏國已付款部分卻被延遲，目前月供約12枚，僅拜登時期四分之一，問題在政治決定而非產能。川普日前簽行政令暫緩實施部分對俄制裁，配合美俄柴油協議，澤倫斯基批此舉錯誤。
當前戰場壓力驟增。俄軍入冬前加大打擊烏國電力設施，多城長時間停電；烏攔截彈有限，星鏈、情資與愛國者任一環鬆動，都直接影響防空能力。澤倫斯基警告風險已逼近海嘯級，但華府優先順序顯已從「撐烏」部分轉向「壓油價、控盤、保談判」。
paras_en: In a Bloomberg interview on Sunday, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky accused the United States of using military aid, satellite communications and energy policy to pressure Kyiv into accepting a cease‑fire that would favor Russia. He stressed he is not claiming this is Washington’s explicit goal, but recent actions “look that way,” and a week‑long public dispute between the two sides has further intensified.

The controversy stems from Ukraine’s strikes on Russian oil refineries and has spilled over into broader issues such as sanctions on Russia, the use of Starlink and military‑grade Starshield services, intelligence sharing, and the supply of Patriot missiles. Zelensky put forward a swap: Ukraine would stop hitting Russia’s diesel‑supply chain, and the United States would increase Patriot interceptors to protect energy facilities and cities. So far, Washington has only demanded that Ukraine cease its attacks and has not accepted the proposed exchange.

The U.S. position is aimed at lowering energy prices and preserving a negotiation channel with Moscow, saying that keeping a Russian diesel‑supply arrangement helps avoid “pushing Putin off the negotiating table,” and it has accused Zelensky of dragging out the war.

Kyiv’s view is that while Russian forces continue to bomb Ukrainian energy infrastructure, the United States is easing economic pressure on Russia, which only weakens the leverage to force Moscow to back down.

The Starlink and intelligence dispute has intensified. Zelensky said that once equipment inside Ukraine exceeded speeds of 161 km/h, service was throttled, pointing the finger at the White House, which denied issuing any such order. He also confirmed that the United States briefly halted the sharing of early‑warning data on Russian ballistic missile launches before restoring it.

At the same time, Patriot deliveries have become another flashpoint: Zelensky said Ukraine has paid for a portion of the missiles but deliveries have been delayed, with the current monthly supply at about 12 units—only a quarter of the rate under the Biden administration. He blamed political decisions rather than production capacity. Former President Trump recently signed an executive order to pause parts of the sanctions regime against Russia, aligning with the U.S.–Russia diesel agreement, a move Zelensky condemned as a mistake.

The pressure on the battlefield has surged. In the run‑up to winter, Russian forces have stepped up attacks on Ukraine’s power grid, causing prolonged blackouts in multiple cities. Ukraine’s interceptor stockpiles are limited, and any slack in Starlink, intelligence or Patriot coverage directly erodes its air‑defence capability. Zelensky warned that the risk is approaching a “tsunami‑level” threat, but the U.S. appears to have shifted its priority from “supporting Ukraine” to “pressuring oil prices, controlling the market, and safeguarding negotiations.”

items.title: 賣出訊號解除！美銀Hartnett看11月中旬重返科技股 關鍵在晶片價格
items.title_en: Sell‑Signal Lifted! BofA’s Hartnett Sees Mid‑November Return to Tech Stocks, Chip Prices Key
paras: 美銀證券策略師Michael Hartnett指出，美銀牛熊指標已跌破警戒門檻，結束先前的賣出訊號，但尚未發出買進訊號。投資人能否在11月中旬重返科技股，關鍵在於晶片價格能否延續漲勢；若價格回落，恐意味AI融資環境進一步收緊、資本支出成長見頂。
Hartnett在最新一期《Flow Show》報告中指出，美銀牛熊指標由8.1降至7.4，跌破8.0門檻，正式結束5月26日觸發的賣出訊號。舊版指標也從5.6降至5.1，兩者均顯示，夏季極度樂觀的市場情緒已告終。
賣出訊號結束 買點仍待確認
指標下滑，主要受到全球股市上漲廣度惡化、避險基金持有原油與標普500期貨空單、黃金期貨多單減少，以及高收益債和新興市場債資金流入轉弱影響。科技股持續吸金，則是唯一推升指標的因素。
不過，賣出訊號終止不代表買點已到。美銀廣度規則顯示，全球股市指數淨超賣比例達52%，為2025年4月以來最高，但仍低於觸發反向買進訊號所需的88%。
Hartnett認為，除非目前仍處於超買狀態的美國、台灣與巴西股市再跌6%至10%，否則短期內難以達到這項門檻。
科技股重挫，資金仍未明顯撤離
儘管那斯達克100指數單週跌幅近6%，資金流向卻未顯示投資人大舉撤出。EPFR截至當週三的數據顯示，股票基金淨流入644億美元，債券基金吸金118億美元，現金則流出531億美元。
美銀私人客戶的股票配置占比達66.4%，創歷史新高，現金占比則降至歷史低點9.3%。今年全球股票基金淨流入金額換算成年率達1.3兆美元，其中科技基金達1960億美元，超過先前紀錄的2.5倍。
美銀10月基金經理人調查也顯示，科技股超配程度為2020年8月以來最高，反映市場情緒雖降溫，投資部位仍高度集中。
韓股的落差尤其明顯。南韓綜合指數(KOSPI) 指數自6月高點下跌30%，但8月資金流入高峰過後，每流入100美元，僅有7美元撤離。
Hartnett指出，外資是當週賣壓主力，加上股票回購窗口接近關閉，真正的撤資可能尚未開始。
AI融資壓力升高，暫守防禦立場
Hartnett目前仍採取防禦策略，並列出重新擁抱風險資產的兩項前提，包括聯準會10月28日升息以恢復信譽，以及AI融資疑慮緩解，但兩者目前均未實現。
市場預期聯準會10月升息的機率，已由逾50%降至14%；AI信貸市場則剛經歷今年最差的一週。CoreWeave債券跌入困境區間，5年期信用違約交換（CDS）利差隱含的五年違約機率約63%。
高盛數據顯示，CoreWeave於2031年到期的債券，與美國公債的利差一度超過1100個基點。甲骨文5年期CDS也急升，但整體投資級科技債利差幾乎未動，顯示高槓桿借款人承受的壓力最大。
此外，美國10年期實質殖利率逼近3%，過去這一水準曾與網路泡沫破裂、全球金融危機及矽谷銀行事件等風險事件相伴出現，也讓Hartnett維持審慎態度。
11月能否回補科技股 晶片價格是關鍵
Hartnett認為，半導體價格將是左右2027年經濟與市場走向的重要變數。高盛數據顯示，半導體生產者物價指數在經歷近30年下行後，近期急劇攀升。
若晶片價格持續上漲，意味美中AI競賽延續，也有助維持市場對美國政府隱性支撐股債價格的預期。在這種情境下，投資人將於11月中旬重返科技股，並在邁入2027年之際，反轉「放空科技股、做多債券」的部位。
反之，若晶片價格回落，可能代表AI信貸進一步收緊、資本支出成長見頂，支撐名目GDP繁榮的動力也將動搖。屆時債券表現可能較佳，仰賴AI資本支出題材支撐估值的資產則將承壓，2027年報酬來源也可能從資本增值轉向收益。
市場共識預估，超大規模雲端業者資本支出將由2026年的8070億美元，增至2027年的1.16兆美元；自由現金流則預計由今年負630億美元，惡化至明年負1630億美元，凸顯融資環境的重要性。
暫不加碼科技股 布局殖利率見頂受惠資產
在操作上，Hartnett暫不加碼科技股，而是增加可能受惠於殖利率見頂的資產，包括小型股、不動產投資信託（REITs）及非必需消費類股。後者在美銀10月調查中的低配程度，為2008年7月以來最高。
長期配置方面，他維持超配黃金、大宗商品與新興市場，但認為應逐步縮減長期放空債券及低配中國的部位。
Hartnett也指出，標普500指數已有355檔成分股較52週高點下跌逾10%，其中188檔跌逾20%、93檔跌逾30%。指數表面之下，個股已承受相當程度的修正，可能為耐心等待布局時機的投資人帶來價值空間。
paras_en: BofA Securities strategist Michael Hartnett said the bank’s bull‑bear indicator has fallen below the warning threshold, ending the previous sell‑signal, but a buy‑signal has not yet been issued. Whether investors can return to tech stocks by mid‑November hinges on whether chip prices can keep rising; a price pull‑back could signal tighter AI financing and a peak in cap‑ex growth.

In the latest “Flow Show” report Hartnett noted the bull‑bear indicator dropped from 8.1 to 7.4, slipping below the 8.0 mark and formally ending the sell‑signal triggered on May 26. The older version of the indicator also fell from 5.6 to 5.1, both showing that the extreme optimism of the summer market mood is over.
Sell‑signal ended, buy‑point still unconfirmed

The indicator’s decline is mainly due to a worsening breadth in global equity markets, hedge funds holding short positions in oil and S&P 500 futures, a reduction in long gold futures, and weaker inflows into high‑yield and emerging‑market debt. Continued inflows into tech stocks are the only factor that still lifts the indicator.

However, the end of the sell‑signal does not mean a buying opportunity has arrived. BofA’s breadth rule shows the net oversold ratio of global equity indices is 52%, the highest since April 2025, but still below the 88% needed to trigger a reverse‑buy signal.
Hartnett believes that unless the currently overbought U.S., Taiwan and Brazil markets fall another 6‑10%, the threshold is unlikely to be met in the short term.
Tech stocks tumble, but capital has not clearly fled

Even though the Nasdaq‑100 fell almost 6% over the week, fund flows did not show a massive investor exodus. EPFR data through Wednesday showed a net inflow of $64.4 billion into equity funds, $11.8 billion into bond funds, and a net outflow of $53.1 billion from cash.

BofA’s private‑client equity allocation reached 66.4%, a historic high, while cash holdings fell to a historic low of 9.3%. Global equity fund net inflows this year amount to an annualised $1.3 trillion, with tech funds alone attracting $196 billion – more than 2.5 times the previous record.
A BofA October survey of fund managers also showed tech‑stock over‑weighting at its highest since August 2020, indicating that despite cooler sentiment, positions remain heavily concentrated.
The gap is especially stark in South Korea. The KOSPI has slid 30% from its June peak, yet after the August inflow peak, every $100 that came in only saw $7 withdrawn.
Hartnett said foreign investors were the main sellers that week, and with the stock‑repurchase window nearing its end, true capital outflows may not have started yet.
AI financing pressure rises, staying defensive for now

Hartnett remains defensive and lists two pre‑conditions for re‑embracing risk assets: a rate hike by the Fed on Oct. 28 to restore credibility, and a easing of AI‑financing concerns – neither of which has materialised yet.

The market’s probability view of an October Fed hike has dropped from over 50% to 14%; the AI credit market just endured its worst week of the year. CoreWeave bonds fell into distress, with the five‑year CDS spread implying a roughly 63% five‑year default probability.

Goldman data show CoreWeave’s 2031 bond spread over U.S. Treasuries once exceeded 11,100 bps. Oracle’s five‑year CDS also spiked, but overall investment‑grade tech‑bond spreads barely moved, indicating that highly‑leveraged borrowers feel the most pressure.

In addition, the real yield on the U.S. 10‑year Treasury is approaching 3%. Historically, that level has coincided with the dot‑com bust, the global financial crisis and the Silicon Valley Bank collapse, prompting Hartnett to stay cautious.
Can chip prices decide a November tech‑stock rebound?

Hartnett believes semiconductor prices will be a decisive factor for the 2027 economic and market outlook. Goldman data show the semiconductor producer price index, after nearly three decades of decline, has recently surged sharply.

If chip prices keep rising, it suggests the U.S.–China AI race continues and helps sustain market expectations of implicit U.S. government support for equity‑bond prices. In that scenario investors would return to tech stocks by mid‑November and, heading into 2027, reverse the “short tech, long bonds” stance.

Conversely, a chip‑price decline could signal tighter AI credit, a cap‑ex peak and a weakening of the drivers behind nominal‑GDP growth. Bonds would likely outperform, while assets that rely on AI‑cap‑ex‑driven valuations would feel pressure, shifting 2027 returns from capital gains to income.

Consensus forecasts estimate that ultra‑large cloud providers’ cap‑ex will rise from $807 billion in 2026 to $1.16 trillion in 2027; free cash flow is projected to worsen from a $63 billion deficit this year to a $163 billion deficit next year, underscoring the importance of financing conditions.
Hold off on adding to tech, favour assets that benefit from a yield‑peak environment

In practice Hartnett is not adding to tech positions now, but is increasing exposure to assets that could benefit from a yield‑peak, such as small‑caps, REITs and consumer‑discretionary stocks. The latter’s under‑weighting in BofA’s October survey is at its highest since July 2008.
For the long run he remains over‑weight in gold, commodities and emerging markets, while recommending a gradual reduction of long‑bond shorts and a low‑weight stance on China.

Hartnett also noted that 355 S&P 500 constituents have fallen more than 10% from their 52‑week highs, with 188 down over 20% and 93 down over 30%. Beneath the index’s surface, individual stocks have endured sizable corrections, potentially offering value opportunities for patient investors waiting to deploy capital.

items.title: 馬斯克秀飛行汽車 大西洋月刊潑冷水「永遠不該造出來」
items.title_en: Musk Shows Flying Car; Atlantic Monthly Douses It With Cold Water, Saying It Should ‘Never Have Been Built’
paras: 《大西洋月刊》評論指出，飛行汽車或許永遠不該被造出來，因為這個延續百年的夢想，作為幻想比化為現實更有吸引力。
特斯拉(TSLA-US) 上周展示特斯拉 Roadster「飛行」原型車，雖然空中特技令人驚豔，卻也凸顯了核心問題：人們追求的究竟是能飛的汽車，還是擺脫道路束縛、永遠被推遲的自由想像？
這輛跑車倒掛在弧形軌道上，利用與 SpaceX(SPCX-US) 合作設計的空氣動力推進器，上演一連串空中特技，包括飛躍一輛特斯拉 Semi 卡車。
展示結束後，馬斯克引用前 PayPal 合夥人提爾（Peter Thiel）的名言：「我們想要的是飛行汽車，結果得到的卻是140個字元。」
這句話出自提爾旗下創投公司 Founders Fund 於2011年發表的科技宣言，批評全球智慧與資金未投入重大挑戰，反而流向推特等社群平台。
這番說法有個矛盾：Founders Fund 當時最重要的投資，正是同屬社群平台的 Facebook。更根本的問題則是，人們真的想要一輛飛行汽車嗎？如同噴射背包，飛行汽車象徵的可能不只是未來，而是透過科技突破實現個人自由。
百年嘗試 始終難以普及
從字面意義來看，飛行汽車並非新鮮夢想。早期實用飛機同樣先在地面滑行，再升空飛行，某種程度上就是長了翅膀的汽車。
1917年，柯蒂斯（Glenn Curtiss）打造配備可拆卸機翼與螺旋槳的 Curtiss Autoplane，卻未能真正有效飛行。沃特曼（Waldo Waterman）1937年的 Arrowbile 在飛行方面更成功，但不具商業可行性。後來的 Taylor Aerocar 雖於1956年取得聯邦政府認證，也始終未能量產。
後續嘗試同樣困難重重。1973年，斯莫林斯基（Henry Smolinski）將塞斯納飛機機翼裝上福特 Pinto，打造 AVE Mizar，卻在試飛事故中喪生。
莫勒（Paul Moller）從1960年代起多次開發可垂直起降的 Skycar，直到公司於2010年代中期陷入停滯。Terrafugia 的 Transition 則長年停留在「再過幾年就上市」的承諾，直到公司於2021年倒閉。
如今，馬斯克也提出時間表，宣稱 Roadster 將在2028年投產，還補上一句「說真的」。
飛越道路 成為自由象徵
評論認為，要理解飛行汽車為何令人著迷，必須回到汽車普及後的社會變化。當汽車在美國成為主流，取代火車與電車等集體交通工具，它也逐漸象徵個人自主權，讓人能獨自前往想去的地方。
然而，這份自由始終受制於道路。即使美國擁有廣闊土地與綿延公路，道路似乎永遠不夠，於是從上方飛越，成了擺脫限制的想像。
早在1923年，科幻先驅根斯巴克（Hugo Gernsback）便構想以陀螺儀驅動的 Helicar，希望將旅客從紐約壅塞街道解放出來。1927年的電影《大都會》讓小型飛行器穿梭城市上空；1962年的動畫《傑森一家》，則進一步將飛行汽車描繪成人人使用的通勤工具。
這些作品承載的共同願望，是當地面生活愈來愈擁擠，天空便成為新自由的寄託。
能短暫離地 不代表能飛行通勤
不過，Roadster 與這些真實或虛構的前輩並不相同。它的空氣風扇系統，主要作用似乎是提高車輪抓地力，搭配車尾火箭推進器，使車輛在展示中從靜止加速至時速60英里，耗時不到一秒。
至於所謂的飛行，更接近桶滾、原地跳躍等空中特技。車輛確實能短暫離地，但是否具備、或打算提供日常旅行與通勤所需的飛行能力，仍不清楚。
為避免造成人員傷亡，這場展示採無人駕駛方式進行。評論作者表示，眼前景象讓他想到的，是富有的機械愛好者在住宅區跳躍、旋轉而製造混亂，而非上班族搭乘飛行汽車往返職場。
真正吸引人的 是尚未實現的夢
任何從道路進入空域的車輛，都面臨龐大監管障礙，但評論認為，法規並非飛行汽車夢想遲遲未能實現的主要原因。更深層的問題是，這個夢想留在幻想中，或許比成為現實更有吸引力。
當汽車帶來的個人自由普及，道路也隨之擠滿奔波的人群，原本象徵自由的公路便成為另一種束縛，上方藍天則再次被賦予逃離現實的希望。即使是提爾口中的飛行汽車，也更像值得追求的象徵，而非真正值得落實的生活方式。
評論最後指出，Roadster 至少在這場展示中展現驚人能力，但它實現百年飛行汽車雄心的方式，是成為特技駕駛的載具，而非一般駕駛的飛行器。它最終滿足的，或許是馬斯克自己的夢想：宣稱交付了前人一個世紀以來都未能交付的事物。
paras_en: The Atlantic Monthly editorial argues that flying cars may never ought to be built, because this century‑old dream is more alluring as a fantasy than as a reality.

Tesla (TSLA‑US) displayed a “flying” prototype of the Roadster last week; while the aerial stunts were impressive, they also highlighted a core question: are people really after a car that can fly, or the freedom of shedding road constraints that has been perpetually postponed?

The sports car was inverted on a curved track and, using an aerodynamic thruster designed in partnership with SpaceX (SPCX‑US), performed a series of aerial maneuvers, including leaping over a Tesla Semi truck.
After the demonstration, Musk quoted former PayPal partner Peter Thiel: “What we wanted was a flying car, and what we got was 140 characters.”

The line comes from a 2011 technology manifesto issued by Thiel’s venture firm Founders Fund, which criticized the global brain‑power and capital being funneled into social platforms like Twitter rather than into major challenges.

The remark is contradictory because Founders Fund’s biggest investment at the time was in another social platform, Facebook. More fundamentally, the piece asks whether people truly want a flying car, or whether, like a jetpack, it symbolizes personal liberty achieved through technological breakthroughs.
A Century‑Long Quest That Has Never Gone Mainstream
Literally, the flying‑car idea is not new. Early practical airplanes also taxied on the ground before taking off, essentially cars with wings.

In 1917 Glenn Curtiss built the Curtiss Autoplane with detachable wings and a propeller, but it never achieved effective flight. Waldo Waterman’s 1937 Arrowbile was more successful in the air but commercially unviable. Later, the Taylor Aerocar earned federal certification in 1956 yet never entered mass production.
Subsequent attempts ran into similar hurdles. In 1973 Henry Smolinski attached Cessna wings to a Ford Pinto to create the AVE Mizar, but the test‑flight ended in a fatal crash.

Paul Moller pursued vertical‑takeoff Skycars from the 1960s until his company stalled in the mid‑2010s. Terrafugia’s Transition lingered for years on promises of a “launch in a few years” before the firm folded in 2021.
Now Musk has set a timetable, claiming the Roadster will go into production in 2028, adding a casual “seriously.”
Flying Over Roads as a Symbol of Freedom

Commentators say that to understand the allure of flying cars one must look back at the social changes after automobiles became ubiquitous. When cars displaced trains and streetcars in the United States, they also came to represent personal autonomy, letting individuals travel wherever they wished.

Yet that freedom remained bounded by roads. Even with America’s vast land and endless highways, the road network always seemed insufficient, prompting the fantasy of soaring above to escape those limits.

As early as 1923, sci‑fi pioneer Hugo Gernsback imagined a gyroscope‑driven Helicar to free passengers from congested New York streets. The 1927 film “Metropolis” showed tiny aircraft zipping over a city, and the 1962 cartoon “The Jetsons” portrayed flying cars as everyday commuter vehicles.
These works share a common wish: as ground‑level life grew more crowded, the sky became a new repository for liberty.
Briefly Leaving the Ground Does Not Equal Commuter‑Ready Flight

However, the Roadster differs from these real or fictional predecessors. Its air‑fan system appears mainly to boost wheel traction, while a rear‑mounted rocket provides thrust that accelerated the vehicle from a standstill to 60 mph in under a second during the demo.

The so‑called “flight” was more akin to barrel rolls and hops in place. The car can lift off momentarily, but whether it possesses—or intends to provide—the sustained flight capability needed for everyday travel remains unclear.

To avoid injuries, the demonstration was conducted unmanned. The author of the commentary likened the spectacle to wealthy gadget enthusiasts jumping and spinning in residential neighborhoods, creating chaos, rather than to commuters using a flying car to get to work.
What Truly Captivates Is the Unfulfilled Dream

Any vehicle that moves from road to air faces massive regulatory hurdles, but the commentary argues that regulation is not the primary reason the flying‑car dream has stalled. A deeper issue is that the fantasy may be more attractive than turning it into reality.

When personal freedom spread through automobiles, roads became crowded with commuters, turning the once‑symbolic highways into another form of constraint, while the blue sky above regained its role as an imagined escape. Even the flying‑car Thiel mentions feels more like a coveted symbol than a practical lifestyle.

The commentary concludes that the Roadster demonstrated astonishing capabilities in this showcase, but its path to fulfilling a century‑old flying‑car ambition is as a stunt platform rather than a conventional aerial vehicle. Ultimately, it may satisfy Musk’s own dream: claiming to have delivered something no one has been able to deliver for a hundred years.

items.title: 【開盤即地獄？】費半連8黑、台股暴跌千點？散戶保命，這兩步千萬別錯！
items.title_en: Opening in Hell? Nasdaq Futures Down 8 Days Straight, Taiwan Stocks Plunge a Thousand Points? Retail Investors Survival: Don’t Miss These Two Steps!
paras: 費半連續8個交易日收黑，創2008年以來最長的連跌紀錄，指數大跌11.4%。外資也沒閒著，連8日賣超，累計超過6,800億元下。今日台股恐怕將出現「千點海嘯」。但這波全球股市回檔，江江要問你一件重要的事：「公司是賺不到錢了，還是大家把價格砍得比較狠？」
其實這波賣壓來自三個擔心：
一、AI投資什麼時候回本
二、企業舉債擴張
三、油價大漲à升息
這些都是「估值」的問題，也就是市場願意為未來付多少錢。它們不是「訂單消失了」的問題。這就好像：你家附近的海鮮攤，今天魚沒壞、冷凍櫃沒停電，只是新聞說「海鮮價格可能太貴」，客人嚇得全跑了。老闆被迫降價清貨，但魚還是那些魚。這就是台股正在發生的事！
如果今天是基本面崩壞，你應該會看到雲端四大巨頭砍資本支出、台積電(2330-TW)接單被取消、輝達(NVDA-US)晶片賣不出去。但現實情況是什麼？

！行情要落底，技術面上必須等待 急跌盤底、出現向上跳空缺口，以及 MACD 柱狀體出現收腳。等訊號確立後再進場，你的資金安全度和勝率會高出許多。

Foreign investors are also active, selling for eight straight days and netting over NT$680 billion. Today Taiwan’s market may see a “thousand‑point tsunami”. Yet this global market pull‑back raises a key question: “Is it that companies can’t make money, or are investors simply cutting prices harder?”
In fact, this selling pressure stems from three concerns:
1. When will AI investments break even?
2. Corporate debt‑financed expansion
3. Surge in oil prices leading to rate hikes

These are all valuation issues – how much the market is willing to pay for future earnings – not a “vanishing order” problem. It’s like a seafood stall near your home: the fish are fresh, the freezers are fine, but a news story says “seafood may be too pricey,” scaring customers away. The owner must slash prices, yet the fish remain the same. That’s what’s happening to Taiwan’s market!
If fundamentals were collapsing, you’d see the four cloud giants cutting capex, TSMC (2330‑TW) losing orders, and Nvidia (NVDA‑US) chips not selling. But what’s the reality?
1. TSMC just reported Q3 earnings up 69% year‑over‑year, and CEO Wei‑Zhe‑Jia clearly said demand for advanced processes “far exceeds supply.”
2. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang also stepped in to reassure, emphasizing that the productivity revolution driven by AI is only just beginning.
3. The four U.S. cloud service providers are raising next year’s capex, even boosting it by 60% to exceed $1.5 trillion.

The data are plain: real AI demand and profit‑driving power haven’t changed. What the market is killing now are the high‑leverage positions that rode a too‑fast rally, a high base and over‑extended financing. Main players, using foreign‑investor selling and short‑term negatives, are staging a “big dump” to wash out weak retail investors!
Facing a thousand‑point tsunami, remember these two survival principles:
1. Don’t blindly chase low‑price stocks. In panic, you often cut the stocks that will post the best earnings next month. Check fundamentals and technicals first; don’t let emotion drive your orders.
2. Don’t rush to bottom‑fish. Staggered positioning is far more important than loading up in one go.

When the market bottoms, you must wait for technical signs: a sharp‑drop bottom, an upward gap, and MACD histogram turning up. Enter only after those signals confirm – your capital safety and win rate will be much higher.
Big players are quietly building positions! Pull‑back locks in these six “excellent‑chip” indicator stocks

When the market is most fearful, it’s the moment for “early‑bird” investors. While retail investors flee, foreign investors, mutual funds and large accounts are already locking in low‑base, high‑growth quality stocks. Below are six well‑positioned indicator stocks worth adding to your watchlist during the pull‑back:
Foreign‑investor lock‑in indicators:

1. Guoguang (6209‑TW): Successfully pivoted to automotive lenses and IoT optics, dramatically improving its product mix. With rising automotive lens shipments and a higher share of high‑margin products, profit structure has strengthened, prompting foreign investors to snap up positions.

2. TaiBiaoTech (6278‑TW): Global leader in SMT assembly, deep‑focused on AI server boards and automotive electronics. Benefiting from strong demand for high‑end boards and expanding low‑earth‑orbit satellite applications, it maintains rapid growth, earning double‑lock‑in from foreign investors and large accounts.
Mutual‑fund lock‑in indicators:

3. Jinxiang Electronics (2368‑TW): Absolute leader in high‑layer AI server PCBs. With massive shipments of 800 Gbps switches and next‑gen AI server boards, average selling price and gross margin keep rising, fueling profit momentum and strong mutual‑fund positioning.

4. Daliu (3167‑TW): High‑end PCB and semiconductor packaging equipment maker, venturing into CoWoS advanced packaging. Riding urgent orders from major semiconductor firms expanding capacity, order visibility is extremely high, and revenue and profit are exploding multiplicatively.
Large‑account lock‑in indicators:

5. Fanquan (6830‑TW): Leader in semiconductor material analysis, a key component for silicon‑photonics CPO and advanced‑process R&D. Benefiting from booming demand for advanced‑process inspection, quarterly revenue hits new highs, attracting large accounts to add on the dip.

6. Zhongda‑KY (4977‑TW): Leading high‑speed optical transceiver module maker, deep in CPO (co‑packaged optics) technology. Driven by AI compute centers’ urgent need for high‑bandwidth transmission, new‑generation product mass‑production brings huge profit‑growth flexibility.
Conclusion: The end of a crash often marks the start of huge profits!

There’s a market adage: “Only those who dare to see opportunity in a crash earn the ensuing gains.” Market sentiment is as changeable as weather, but industry long‑term trends are like the seasons – inevitable. When a plunge pushes quality stocks back near their long‑term averages, it becomes the best gift for rational investors.

Reminder: Don’t let emotion make decisions! Preserve capital, stay calm, and stagger purchases of low‑base, strong‑chip stocks. When a gap appears and sentiment warms, you’ll thank your cool, wise self!

paras_en: Last Friday (10/16), all four major US indices closed lower: the Dow fell 175 points, the S&P 500 dropped 1.09%, the Nasdaq plunged 2.15%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index tumbled 3.83%, marking eight consecutive trading days of declines and an 11.4% weekly loss!

Three main reasons were cited: first, the market worries that AI companies are over‑leveraged and future returns may not support massive capex; second, breakthroughs in Chinese memory‑chip technology raise concerns about future supply increases; third, the US‑Iran conflict is heating up, with Brent crude nearing $110, reigniting inflation and rate‑hike pressures. However, the US 10‑year Treasury yield has slipped to around 5.1%, and the market still sees an 82% chance the Fed will hold rates steady at the end of October, meaning further hikes are not a foregone conclusion.

On the technical side, the S&P 500 closed at 7,659, breaking the 7,700 support level. Short‑term focus is on whether 7,600 can hold, while the 7,700‑7,800 zone now acts as resistance. International futures also flashed warning signs: Japan’s Nikkei 225 futures fell 1,890 points in overnight trading, and South Korea’s KOSPI200 futures dropped 3.5% on Friday.

Global equities have clearly turned weaker in the short term, but corporate fundamentals have not deteriorated across the board. If US‑Iran tensions ease and oil prices retreat, confidence could rebound. Until semiconductor stocks confirm a bottom, investors should stay vigilant and avoid rushing in for a rebound!
Taiwan futures plunged 1,144 points in overnight trading! Foreign investors’ short positions neared 100,000 contracts, and a 46,000‑contract defense battle looms on Monday!

Taiwan’s market surged 551 points at one point on Friday, peaking at 47,520, but heavy selling in the final session limited the gain to 141 points, closing at 47,111 with a turnover of NT$935.9 billion. Notably, foreign investors have been net sellers for eight straight days and sold another NT$46.1 billion on Friday; futures net short positions remain high at 93,600 contracts, indicating that foreign hedging and bearish positioning are still ongoing!
Hit by the US tech sell‑off, Taiwan futures dropped 1,144 points overnight on Friday, closing at 46,140, and TSMC futures fell 47 points, suggesting heavy selling pressure on Monday!

But falling stock prices do not mean earnings are falling. TSMC (2330) posted Q3 EPS of NT$29.43, up 68.7% YoY, and forecasts Q4 US revenue of $52.3‑$54.3 billion, with full‑year US revenue growth now revised up to 44%, confirming strong demand for advanced AI processes. items.title: 「不是債市太悲觀就是股市太樂觀！」 高盛警告背離近臨界點：AI股恐再跌15%  點名對沖台灣半導體
items.title_en: "Either the bond market is too pessimistic or the stock market is too optimistic!" Goldman Sachs warns divergence nearing a tipping point: AI stocks may fall another 15% and names Taiwan semiconductor hedge
paras: 美國股市與信貸市場對AI題材的定價，正出現明顯裂口。高盛出具最新研報指出，AI超大型雲端廠商(hyperscaler)的信貸利差已擴大至年內最寬，但對應股價尚未充分反映壓力。
高盛策略師Louis Miller指出，市場正面臨二選一，「不是債市悲觀過頭，就是股市還有約15%下行空間未被消化。」
高盛AI超大型雲端廠商信貸利差指數(GSUCHS30)上週升至今年新高。Miller指出，7月利差接近此水準時，相關股票價格較現行水準低約15%。
此外，高盛AI受益股籃子相對「剔除AI成分」的標普500指數，已自6月高點回落約25%。信貸市場通常對現金流、融資成本與違約風險更敏感，這次率先反應，顯示市場辯論核心已從「AI需求有多強」轉向「資本支出能否回收」。
壓力不只在雲廠。超大型雲端廠商信用違約交換(CDS)觸及歷史新高，更下層的垃圾債市場中，20檔AI資料中心債券中有7檔還款來源依賴單一租戶CoreWeave，而CoreWeave債券殖利率已飆至15%左右、落入困境級區間。高盛認為，這是AI融資鏈從核心向外圍蔓延的訊號。
核心解釋在資本支出增速觸頂。高盛估算，超大型雲端廠商資本支出年增率約在今年第三季見頂(116%)，之後逐季放緩，2027年底降至約20%，重點不在總額立刻下滑，而在市場過去按「持續加速」給估值，一旦增速轉平，回報假設就要重算。
與此同時，折舊反噬是下一顆未爆彈。高盛測算，超大型雲端廠商資本支出扣除折舊後淨值，對標普EPS成長的貢獻，2026年約+11個百分點、2027年降至+7個百分點，2028年隨大量資料中心資產進入攤提高峰，貢獻轉為-1個百分點，原本支撐高獲利的AI投資，增速過後會變成利潤表拖累。
市場內部指標也同步轉弱。看跌選擇權成交量上週五(16日)升至年內次高水位；高盛高貝塔因子組合較高點跌15%；周期股相對防禦股隱含經濟成長預期降至約2%；避險基金貝塔調整後淨部位處在五年第67百分位、淨槓桿僅第17百分位，顯示「想跟AI順勢」但槓桿沒跟上。金融條件由正轉負，更高利率與更寬利差直接壓負債依賴股。
不過，Miller並未斷言指數崩盤，而是稱市場正以輪動消化壓力，並給出五項應對策略：一、做多剔除AI的寬基市場，AI與非AI相關性已轉負；二、做多品質因子但防技術面過熱，質量因子三個月漲20%、RSI破80；三、中期醫療保健，押ACA補貼延長帶動就醫流量；四、做多巴西非相關機會，總統決選舉行前後估值有重估空間；五、對沖台灣半導體部位，因台積電調高指引後股價仍偏弱，亞洲團隊建議做空台灣半導體籃子。
對投資人而言，高盛這份周報的重點不是「AI結束」，而是定價階段切換：股價還在講成長，債市已開始算折舊與融資成本。若信貸利差續擴，AI概念股補跌風險將從邊緣租戶、NeoCloud、光通訊與記憶體鏈，逐步回推至核心雲巨頭與半導體龍頭。
paras_en: The pricing of AI themes in U.S. equities and credit markets is showing a clear split. Goldman Sachs' latest research note says credit spreads for AI hyperscale cloud providers have widened to the widest level this year, yet stock prices have not yet fully reflected the pressure.
Goldman strategist Louis Miller notes the market faces a binary choice: "Either the bond market is overly pessimistic, or the stock market still has about 15% downside not yet priced in."

The Goldman AI hyperscale cloud credit spread index (GSUCHS30) rose to a new high for the year last week. Miller points out that when spreads were near this level in July, the related stock prices were roughly 15% lower than current levels.

Moreover, the basket of AI beneficiary stocks relative to the S&P 500 "excluding AI components" has fallen about 25% from its June peak. Credit markets, which are more sensitive to cash flow, financing costs and default risk, reacted first, indicating the debate has shifted from "how strong AI demand is" to "whether capital spending can be recouped."

The pressure isn’t limited to cloud providers. Credit default swaps on hyperscale cloud firms hit historic highs, and in the junk bond market, 7 of 20 AI data‑center bonds rely on a single tenant, CoreWeave, whose bond yields have surged to roughly 15% and entered distressed territory. Goldman sees this as a signal that AI financing is spreading from the core to the periphery.

The core issue is a peak in capital‑expenditure growth. Goldman estimates hyperscale cloud cap‑ex annual growth will top out in Q3 this year at about 116%, then slow each quarter, falling to roughly 20% by the end of 2027. The focus isn’t an immediate drop in total spend, but the market’s valuation built on a "continuous acceleration" narrative, which must be re‑calculated once growth flattens.

At the same time, depreciation backlash is the next hidden bomb. Goldman calculates that after subtracting depreciation, the net contribution of hyperscale cloud cap‑ex to S&P EPS growth will be about +11 percentage points in 2026, drop to +7 points in 2027, and turn negative (‑1 point) in 2028 as massive data‑center assets hit peak amortization, turning what once supported high AI profits into a profit‑and‑loss drag.

Internal market indicators are also weakening. Put‑option volume rose to the second‑highest level of the year last Friday (the 16th); Goldman’s high‑beta factor portfolio is down 15% from its peak; cyclical stocks’ implied growth expectations relative to defensive stocks have fallen to about 2%; hedge‑fund beta‑adjusted net positions sit at the 67th percentile of the past five years and net leverage at the 17th percentile, showing a desire to ride the AI wave without sufficient leverage. Financial conditions have turned negative, with higher rates and wider spreads directly squeezing debt‑heavy stocks.

However, Miller does not predict a full index collapse. He says the market is rotating to absorb pressure and outlines five strategies: 1) go long the broad market excluding AI, as AI‑related and non‑AI assets are now negatively correlated; 2) go long quality factors while avoiding an overheated tech side—quality factors have risen 20% in three months and RSI has broken 80; 3) mid‑term healthcare, betting on extended ACA subsidies driving patient volume; 4) go long Brazil’s non‑correlated opportunities, where valuation could be reset around the presidential election; 5) hedge Taiwan semiconductor exposure, as TSMC’s stock remains weak despite raised guidance, with the Asian team recommending shorting a Taiwan semiconductor basket.

For investors, the key takeaway from Goldman’s weekly note isn’t that "AI is over," but that the pricing phase is shifting: stocks are still talking growth, while the bond market is already pricing depreciation and financing costs. If credit spreads keep widening, the risk of further AI‑related stock pull‑backs will move from edge tenants, NeoCloud, optical‑communication and memory chains back toward core cloud giants and semiconductor leaders.

items.title: 破天荒！韓媒：三星將採台積電3奈米製程  為輝達生產下一代HBM基底裸片
items.title_en: Breaking Ground! Korean Media: Samsung to Use TSMC 3nm Process for Nvidia's Next-Gen HBM Base Dies
paras: 外媒最新報導指出，南韓三星電子將打破長達數年的「一站式全包」生產模式，採用台積電的3奈米製程，為輝達下一代HBM製造基底裸片(base die)。
韓媒《首爾經濟日報》今(18)日引述消息人士報導，輝達已向三星、SK海力士及美光三家供應商提出統一要求，基底裸片必須使用台積電3奈米工製成，核心裸片則統一採用第六代DRAM工藝(1c)，這一要求源於各供應商製造方案差異導致性能不穩，標準化可大幅減輕輝達的驗證工作量。
報道指出，三星設備解決方案事業部經內部評估後，決定接受輝達要求。三星此次調整僅針對輝達客製化的HBM4E產品。對於標準版HBM及面向超微等其他客戶的產品，三星仍將保留全包生產策略。
目前，三星已全球率先量產第六代HBM4，第七代HBM4E正進行量產驗證，兩款產品的基底裸片均採用三星自研4奈米製程。
值得注意的是，三星並未完全放棄自主生產能力。一位業內人士透露，三星正同步驗證能否在自有產線製造輝達HBM基底裸片，作為防範台積電產能不足的備案，此舉顯示在AI晶片競爭白熱化下，三星正以靈活策略平衡技術自主與客戶需求。
paras_en: Foreign media reports that South Korea's Samsung Electronics will break its years‑long "single‑source full‑pack" production model and adopt TSMC’s 3‑nanometer process to make the base dies for Nvidia’s next‑generation HBM.

Korean outlet Seoul Economic Daily cited sources saying Nvidia has issued a unified request to its three suppliers—Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron—that the base dies be fabricated with TSMC’s 3nm technology, while the core dies use a sixth‑generation DRAM process (1c). The demand stems from performance instability caused by differing manufacturing approaches, and standardisation would greatly reduce Nvidia’s validation workload.

The report says Samsung’s Equipment Solutions division, after an internal review, decided to meet Nvidia’s request. The adjustment applies only to Nvidia‑customised HBM4E products; for standard‑edition HBM and products for other customers such as AMD, Samsung will retain its full‑pack production strategy.

Samsung is currently the first worldwide to mass‑produce sixth‑generation HBM4, and seventh‑generation HBM4E is undergoing volume‑production qualification. Both products’ base dies are made with Samsung’s own 4‑nanometer process.

It is noteworthy that Samsung has not completely abandoned its own manufacturing capability. An industry insider disclosed that Samsung is simultaneously testing whether it can produce Nvidia’s HBM base dies on its own lines as a contingency in case TSMC capacity falls short, showing that amid the fierce AI‑chip battle Samsung is using a flexible strategy to balance technological independence with customer needs.

不過，賣出訊號終止不代表買點已到。美銀廣度規則顯示，全球股市指數淨超賣比例達52%，為2025年4月以來最高，但仍低於觸發反向買進訊號所需的88%。
