items.title: 美股繁榮是假象？AI泡沫疑慮升溫 標普500恐面臨30%修正
items.title_en: Is US Stock Market Prosperity an Illusion? AI Bubble Concerns Rise, S&P 500 May Face a 30% Correction
paras: 標普500指數10月中旬仍徘徊在7,600點上方高位區間，那斯達克與科技巨頭繼續主導市場敘事。表面繁榮之下，市場內部結構已出現深刻分化。前雷曼兄弟交易員、Bear Traps Report創辦人Larry McDonald提出的核心判斷——指數層面尚未充分反映的「內部崩盤」、被動投資的暗面、AI資本開支的不可持續性，以及硬資產與長久期債券的相對吸引力——在最新市場數據中得到部分印證，也引發對未來一至三年資產配置邏輯的重新審視。
當前市場最顯著的結構特徵是市值加權指數與多數成分股表現的嚴重背離。標普500中科技板塊權重長期接近或超過50%，前兩大權重股（輝達與蘋果）合計佔比一度接近13%。同時，大量知名品牌——Nike、麥當勞、家得寶、哈雷戴維森等消費與工業標的——自高點回落30%至80%。2026年10月中旬的市場數據繼續顯示，那斯達克與半導體板塊出現明顯調整，而指數整體仍維持相對韌性。

這種背離並非偶然。被動資金持續流入迫使指數基金與ETF不斷買入權重最大的少數股票，形成自我強化循環。當市場處於上漲年份且指數漲幅達到兩位數時，年末稅務損失賣出與機構調倉往往進一步加劇「強者恆強、弱者更弱」的格局。結果是：指數創下或接近歷史高位，而更廣泛的經濟與企業基本面卻已承壓。消費者層面，油價與中長期利率的顯著上行已構成實際購買力衝擊，連鎖消費與耐用品企業的業績與估值同步承壓，正是這一內部壓力的直接體現。
從歷史比較看，2000年科技泡沫與2007年金融危機前均出現過類似「指數掩蓋內部裂痕」的現象。當時權重集中度遠低於今日，而今日被動資金體量與算法交易的放大效應，使集中度風險更加突出。一旦權重股出現同步調整，指數層面的回撤可能遠超多數投資者的預期。
AI主題仍是驅動科技巨頭與指數的核心敘事，但資本開支的規模與回報週期已引發越來越多的質疑。超大規模科技公司與「新雲端」資料中心運營商持續大規模舉債與股權融資，用於算力、電力與土地投入。2026年下半年，部分資料中心相關債券與可轉債出現明顯拋售，CoreWeave等標的股價與信用利差同步惡化，被視為早期警示信號。

更深層的問題在於估值與退出機制。Anthropic、OpenAI等公司的估值從數年前的千億級躍升至數萬億級，一旦通過IPO或二級市場退出，零售與401(k)資金將在一定程度上成為接盤方。這與2000年前後科技股IPO潮存在結構性相似：早期投資者鎖定利潤，而後期進入者承擔更高估值風險。同時，AI相關資本開支對當期自由現金流形成顯著擠壓，部分巨頭從高自由現金流狀態轉向中性甚至負值，進一步放大了市場對「回報何時兌現」的疑慮。
輝達(NVDA-US)作為算力核心受益者，其估值與市值對指數影響巨大。晶片迭代加速、競爭加劇與客戶資本開支可能放緩，使未來兩到三年出現顯著估值回歸的概率上升。若這一情景兌現，指數層面30%級別的調整並非不可想象，而此後可能進入類似2000至2010年的長時間橫盤整理。
與股票市場形成鮮明對比的是債券市場的深度調整。2017至2021年超低利率環境下發行的大量長期公司債，在利率中樞顯著抬升後價格大幅下跌。以蘋果為例，部分低票息長期債券交易價格曾一度接近面值的一半。這類債券在利率回落情景下具備可觀的資本利得空間，疊加票息後的年化回報有望接近甚至超過部分股票的長期預期收益。
銀行業層面，商業地產貸款再融資壓力與低息存款流失風險並存。零利率時代積累的低成本存款在貨幣市場基金與穩定幣競爭下面臨流出壓力，進一步壓縮淨息差。歐洲銀行對主權債敞口的波動也提示全球固定收益市場的聯動風險。若長端利率出現階段性衝高後的反轉，長久期優質債券與國債有望成為重要的避險與收益來源。
長期來看，更高的通膨中樞與利率環境有利於控制實物資產的企業。1968至1981年高通膨與高利率週期中，工業、材料與能源在標普500中的權重曾達到約50%。當前這些板塊合計權重僅十餘個百分點。家庭財富中配置於商品與相關股票的比例也遠低於歷史高點。
銅、天然氣、石油服務與礦業公司不僅受益於AI資料中心與全球電力基礎設施建設，也受益於新興市場（尤其是印度）的能源與空調需求增長。即便AI資本開支出現階段性放緩，財富從高估值成長股向低估值硬資產的再配置本身就能提供支撐。自由現金流收益率較高、且持續回購的能源與材料公司，在風險回報比上往往優於高估值科技股。
黃金與白銀的表現進一步印證了這一邏輯。中央銀行持續購金、地緣政治不確定性與對主權信用的長期擔憂，使黃金在2026年維持高位運行。穩定幣規模已達約3,000億美元量級，其底層資產大量配置短期國債，客觀上增加了對美元短期債務的需求，卻也強化了金融壓抑與硬資產配置的吸引力。
美國聯邦債務規模龐大，單純依靠傳統手段難以持續。穩定幣的擴張、潛在的收益率曲線控制工具，以及黃金儲備的會計重估等「工具箱」選項，均指向某種形式的金融壓抑——通過機制設計壓低實際利率、引導資金進入特定資產。戰後初期聯準會與財政部的緊密協作提供了歷史參照。這類政策若落地，將進一步推動資金從純金融資產向硬資產與實物資產轉移。
同時，政治週期與中期選舉前後的政策不確定性，也可能成為市場波動的催化劑。無論是對AI資本開支的監管壓力，還是對財政可持續性的重新定價，都可能加速當前高度集中的市場結構發生調整。
在高度集中的市場環境下，單純持有市值加權指數已難以提供充分分散。等權重指數、主動構建的硬資產傾斜組合、精選長久期優質債券，以及具備資料護城河的細分AI應用領域（如醫療機器人、油氣服務資料平台），構成更具韌性的配置方向。稅務損失賣出後的反彈窗口、被過度拋售的優質品牌，也提供了階段性機會。
風險提示同樣明確：AI主題的調整若引發連鎖反應，可能短暫拖累硬資產需求預期；利率若繼續超預期上行，將加劇銀行業與消費端壓力；政策干預的力度與時點存在高度不確定性。投資者需在承認集中度風險的同時，避免簡單的全面做空，而應聚焦估值與現金流的相對優勢。
市場從不會以線性方式兌現風險。當前指數高位與內部裂痕並存的格局，更接近2000年前後的結構特徵，而非單一泡沫的簡單重演。被動投資的規模效應放大了權重股的影響力，也延緩了調整的全面展開。真正的風險不在於是否調整，而在於調整時投資者是否已提前完成從「指數跟隨」向「結構區分」的轉變。硬資產、現金流與合理估值，將成為下一階段更具確定性的錨點。
paras_en: The S&P 500 was still hovering above the 7,600‑point high‑range in mid‑October, while the Nasdaq and tech giants continued to dominate market narrative. Beneath the surface prosperity, the market’s internal structure has become sharply divided. Former Lehman trader and Bear Traps Report founder Larry McDonald’s core thesis – an “internal collapse” not yet reflected at the index level, the dark side of passive investing, the unsustainability of AI capital spending, and the relative appeal of hard assets and long‑duration bonds – finds partial confirmation in the latest data and prompts a reassessment of asset‑allocation logic for the next one to three years.

The most striking structural feature today is the severe divergence between the market‑cap‑weighted index and the performance of most constituents. The tech sector’s weight in the S&P 500 has long been near or above 50%, with the two largest holdings (Nvidia and Apple) at one point approaching 13% combined. At the same time, many well‑known consumer and industrial brands – Nike, McDonald’s, Home Depot, Harley‑Davidson and others – have fallen 30% to 80% from their peaks. Mid‑October 2026 data still show a clear pullback in the Nasdaq and semiconductor sector, while the overall index remains relatively resilient.

This divergence is not accidental. Ongoing inflows into passive funds force index funds and ETFs to keep buying the few highest‑weight stocks, creating a self‑reinforcing loop. In years when the market rises and the index posts double‑digit gains, year‑end tax‑loss selling and institutional rebalancing further amplify a “the strong get stronger, the weak get weaker” pattern. The result: the index reaches or nears historic highs while the broader economy and corporate fundamentals are under pressure. On the consumer side, higher oil prices and rising medium‑ to long‑term rates have eroded real purchasing power, squeezing chain‑store and durable‑goods companies’ earnings and valuations – a direct manifestation of this internal strain.

Historically, similar “index‑masking‑internal‑cracks” episodes appeared before the 2000 tech bubble and the 2007 financial crisis. Back then, weight concentration was far lower than today, but today’s massive passive capital and algorithmic‑trading amplification make concentration risk even more pronounced. If the heavyweight stocks adjust in sync, the index‑level drawdown could far exceed most investors’ expectations.

The AI theme still drives tech giants and the index, but the scale of capital spending and the length of payback periods are drawing increasing skepticism. Mega‑tech firms and “new‑cloud” data‑center operators continue to raise large amounts of debt and equity to fund compute, power and land. In the second half of 2026, some data‑center‑related bonds and convertibles saw noticeable selling; stocks such as CoreWeave and their credit spreads deteriorated, being viewed as early warning signs.

A deeper issue lies in valuations and exit mechanisms. Companies like Anthropic and OpenAI have seen valuations jump from the hundred‑billion to the tens‑of‑trillions dollar range in just a few years. If they exit via IPO or secondary markets, retail and 401(k) funds will become the buyers to some extent. This mirrors the tech‑IPO wave around 2000: early investors lock in profits while later entrants shoulder higher valuation risk. At the same time, AI‑related capex is squeezing current free‑cash‑flow, pushing some giants from strong free‑cash‑flow positions to neutral or even negative, heightening doubts about when returns will materialize.

Nvidia (NVDA‑US), as the core beneficiary of compute power, has an outsized impact on valuation and market‑cap weight. Accelerating chip cycles, intensifying competition and a possible slowdown in customer capex raise the probability of a significant valuation reversion over the next two to three years. If that scenario plays out, a 30%‑level correction at the index level is not unimaginable, after which the market could enter a prolonged sideways consolidation similar to 2000‑2010.

In stark contrast to equities, the bond market has undergone a deep correction. Long‑dated corporate bonds issued in the ultra‑low‑rate environment of 2017‑2021 have seen prices plunge sharply after central rates rose markedly. For example, some low‑coupon Apple long‑term bonds traded at roughly half of par. These bonds offer substantial capital‑gain potential if rates fall, and when combined with coupon yields their annualized return could approach or even exceed the long‑term expected returns of many stocks.

In banking, commercial‑real‑estate loan refinancing pressure coexists with the risk of low‑rate deposit outflows. Low‑cost deposits accumulated in the zero‑interest era face outflows to money‑market funds and stablecoins, further compressing net interest margins. European banks’ sovereign‑debt exposure volatility also highlights global fixed‑income linkage risk. Should long‑end rates spike and then reverse, high‑quality long‑duration bonds and sovereigns could become key hedges and return sources.

Over the long run, higher inflation cores and rate environments favor companies that control physical assets. During the high‑inflation, high‑rate cycle of 1968‑1981, industrials, materials and energy together accounted for about 50% of the S&P 500. Today those sectors together make up only a little over ten percent. The share of household wealth allocated to commodities and related equities is also far below historic peaks.

Copper, natural gas, oil‑service and mining firms benefit not only from AI data‑centers and global power‑infrastructure builds but also from growing energy and air‑conditioning demand in emerging markets, especially India. Even if AI capex eases temporarily, the reallocation of wealth from over‑valued growth stocks to undervalued hard assets can provide support. Energy and materials companies with high free‑cash‑flow yields and ongoing share buybacks often offer a better risk‑adjusted return than lofty‑valued tech stocks.

Gold and silver performance further validates this logic. Central‑bank gold purchases, geopolitical uncertainty and long‑term concerns about sovereign credit have kept gold near its 2026 highs. Stablecoin assets have reached roughly $300 billion, with underlying holdings heavily weighted to short‑term Treasuries, which objectively boosts demand for short‑term US debt while also reinforcing the appeal of financial repression and hard‑asset allocation.

The sheer size of US federal debt makes reliance on traditional tools unsustainable. The expansion of stablecoins, potential yield‑curve control mechanisms and accounting re‑valuation of gold reserves constitute a “toolbox” pointing toward a form of financial repression – designing mechanisms to push real rates lower and steer capital into specific assets. The close post‑World‑War‑II coordination between the Fed and Treasury offers a historical precedent. If such policies materialize, they would further shift capital from pure financial assets toward hard and real assets.

At the same time, political cycles and policy uncertainty around mid‑term elections can act as catalysts for market volatility. Whether through regulatory pressure on AI capex or a repricing of fiscal sustainability, such factors could accelerate adjustments in today’s highly concentrated market structure.

In a highly concentrated market environment, simply holding a market‑cap‑weighted index no longer provides adequate diversification. Equal‑weight indices, actively built hard‑asset‑tilted portfolios, carefully selected long‑duration high‑quality bonds, and niche AI applications with data moats (e.g., medical robotics, oil‑and‑gas service data platforms) represent more resilient allocation paths. Post‑tax‑loss‑sale rebound windows and oversold quality brands also offer tactical opportunities.

Risk warnings are clear: an AI‑theme correction that triggers a chain reaction could briefly dampen hard‑asset demand expectations; rates rising faster than expected would heighten pressure on banks and consumers; and the scale and timing of policy intervention remain highly uncertain. Investors should acknowledge concentration risk but avoid a blanket short‑sell approach, focusing instead on relative valuation and cash‑flow advantages.

Markets never realize risk in a linear fashion. The current coexistence of high index levels and internal cracks resembles the structural features of the early‑2000s rather than a simple replay of a single bubble. The scale effect of passive investing amplifies heavyweight influence and delays a full‑blown correction. The real risk lies not in whether a correction occurs, but whether investors have already shifted from “index‑following” to “structural‑distinction” before it does. Hard assets, cash flow and sensible valuations will become the next‑stage anchors of certainty.

items.title: 烏克蘭命運由三強決定？普丁邀川普、習近平談停戰 排除澤倫斯基
items.title_en: Ukraine's Fate Decided by Three Powers? Putin Invites Trump and Xi to Discuss Ceasefire, Excluding Zelensky
paras: 《華爾街日報》引述消息人士報導，俄羅斯總統普丁提議，下月與美國總統川普及中國國家主席習近平會面，討論烏克蘭問題，試圖協商出有利於莫斯科的方案，結束這場延續四年的戰爭。
這項提議顯示，普丁正試圖趁美俄領袖關係回暖之際推進自身目標，兩人關係升溫已讓烏克蘭及其在華府和歐洲的盟友感到不安。
若在烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基未參與的情況下舉行這類峰會，將是前所未見的安排，也將讓歐洲各國乃至其他地區拉響警報。
一名聽取相關簡報的俄羅斯前情報官員表示，普丁在10月9日與川普通話時提出這項構想。雙方也在那次通話中達成協議，由美國購買俄羅斯柴油，並協助其銷往全球市場。
克里姆林宮發言人佩斯科夫證實，各方正就可能舉行的會議進行討論。
他向《華爾街日報》表示：「目前對於會議本身或可能的議程，都還沒有明確共識，不過三方均承認，理論上有可能舉行這樣的會議。」
一名美國高階官員表示，川普尚未同意出席這類峰會。不過，考量到川普希望兌現結束戰爭的競選承諾，他可能願意接受這項構想。
川普曾宣稱，會在新任期的「第一天」結束戰爭，如今他上任卻已將近兩年。
消息人士指出，克里姆林宮建議，在即將登場的亞太經濟合作會議（APEC）峰會期間，另行舉行三方對話。這場峰會將於11月18日至19日在中國南方科技重鎮深圳舉行。
研究中國的分析人士表示，若三方對話在中國舉行，將是習近平提升中國外交斡旋地位的一大進展。其他熟悉近期俄中磋商的人士透露，俄方官員已透過外交管道向北京提出構想，中方則表示，只要川普同意，就不會反對。
華府智庫史汀生中心中國計畫主任孫韻表示：「中國希望被視為大國之間的樞紐，也可能成為美俄之間的調停者。」
白宮不予置評，中國駐美大使館也未回應置評請求。
上述俄羅斯前情報官員表示，普丁過去也曾向川普和習近平提議舉行三方峰會，但這次提議的背景，是莫斯科與華府的關係出現轉機。
川普剛與普丁達成購買俄羅斯柴油的協議，希望藉此壓低燃料價格。高油價已拖累美國經濟，也衝擊共和黨在期中選舉前的選情。
上周五，川普暫停執行他上月簽署的一項跨黨派法案所規定的對俄制裁，引發國會議員批評，其中包括部分盟友。白宮高階官員表示，川普是在認為幾乎沒有其他有效降價選項後，才做出這些決定。
能源專家普遍認為，伊朗戰爭才是柴油價格上漲的主因，而俄羅斯承諾出售的燃料數量，不足以對市場產生太大影響。
與此同時，川普再度表達對澤倫斯基的不滿，要求烏克蘭停止攻擊俄羅斯煉油廠，並暗示烏克蘭需要一位新總統。美國主導的停戰斡旋則大致陷入停滯。
烏克蘭周日稍早攻擊普丁家鄉聖彼得堡的一座石油碼頭後，川普隨即在Truth Social發文抨擊澤倫斯基。
他指控這位烏克蘭領袖鎖定俄羅斯柴油煉製設施發動攻擊，並稱澤倫斯基「不想結束這場戰爭，而且可能從來就不想」。
川普表示，他暫緩實施制裁，是因為不想讓俄羅斯退出談判。他寫道：「我要這場戰爭結束。」
莫斯科將可能舉行的三方對話，視為鞏固俄羅斯全球強權地位的途徑。這也是普丁自2000年入主克里姆林宮以來，一直追求的地位。
這種會議形式也將歐洲排除在外，而克里姆林宮認為，歐洲是俄羅斯在烏克蘭取得勝利的主要障礙。
俄羅斯前情報官員表示，普丁對三方會談抱持宏大、卻不切實際的企圖，希望將其打造為第二次雅爾達峰會，藉此劃分全球勢力範圍。
即使習近平和川普不太可能同意這種安排，美、俄、中三國領袖共同談判另一個國家命運的畫面，仍將釋出強烈訊號。
不過，這場峰會對習近平而言也並非毫無風險。部分熟悉討論的人士表示，中國官員擔心，這場地緣政治插曲可能喧賓奪主，掩蓋北京原本希望透過APEC展現中國區域角色的安排。
上述人士指出，習近平正試圖在持續支持普丁與維繫中國對歐經濟關係之間，小心拿捏平衡。這類三方會談可能讓中國更直接捲入烏克蘭戰爭，也可能引發歐洲各國反彈；歐洲原本就對北京偏向莫斯科的立場抱持戒心。
paras_en: The Wall Street Journal, citing sources, reports that Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed meeting next month with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss the Ukraine issue, seeking a Moscow-favorable solution to end the four-year war.
The proposal shows Putin is trying to push his agenda while U.S.-Russia relations warm, a development that has made Ukraine and its allies in Washington and Europe uneasy.
Holding such a summit without Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky would be unprecedented and would set off alarms across Europe and elsewhere.

A former Russian intelligence officer who briefed on the matter said Putin raised the idea during a Mandarin‑language call with Trump on Oct. 9, and the two also agreed that the U.S. would purchase Russian diesel and help ship it worldwide.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed that the parties are discussing a possible meeting.
He told the Wall Street Journal, "There is no clear consensus yet on the meeting itself or its agenda, but all three sides acknowledge that, in theory, such a meeting could take place."
A senior U.S. official said Trump has not yet agreed to attend such a summit, but given his desire to fulfill a campaign promise to end the war, he might be willing to consider it.
Trump has claimed he will end the war on the "first day" of his new term, yet he is now approaching two years into his presidency.
Sources say the Kremlin suggested holding a three‑way dialogue during the upcoming APEC summit, which will be held Nov. 18‑19 in Shenzhen, China’s high‑tech hub in the south.

China analysts note that a trilateral dialogue in China would boost Xi’s diplomatic stature, and insiders familiar with recent Russia‑China talks say Russian officials have floated the idea through diplomatic channels, with Beijing saying it would not object if Trump agrees.
Sun Yun, director of the China program at the Stimson Center, said, "China wants to be seen as a hub among great powers and could even become a mediator between the U.S. and Russia."
The White House declined to comment, and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment.
The former intelligence officer added that Putin had previously suggested a three‑way summit to Trump and Xi, but this time the backdrop is a turning point in U.S.–Russia relations.
Trump recently struck a diesel‑purchase deal with Putin, hoping to lower fuel prices; high oil prices have weighed on the U.S. economy and hurt Republican prospects ahead of the midterms.

Last Friday, Trump paused enforcement of a bipartisan sanctions law against Russia that he signed last month, drawing criticism from members of Congress, including some allies. A senior White House official said Trump acted only after concluding there were few other effective ways to cut prices.
Energy experts generally attribute the diesel price surge to the Iran war, noting that the volume Russia has pledged to sell is too small to move the market significantly.

At the same time, Trump reiterated his displeasure with Zelensky, demanding Ukraine stop attacks on Russian refineries and hinting Ukraine needs a new president. U.S.-led cease‑fire mediation has largely stalled.
After Ukraine struck a Russian oil terminal in St. Petersburg earlier on Sunday, Trump immediately posted on Truth Social criticizing Zelensky.
He accused the Ukrainian leader of targeting Russian diesel‑refining facilities and said Zelensky "doesn't want to end the war and may never have wanted to."
Trump said he delayed sanctions because he didn't want Russia to walk away from negotiations, writing, "I want this war to end."
Moscow sees a possible three‑way dialogue as a way to cement Russia’s global great‑power status, a goal Putin has pursued since taking the Kremlin in 2000.
Such a format would also sideline Europe, which the Kremlin views as the main obstacle to a Russian victory in Ukraine.
The former intelligence officer said Putin’s grand but unrealistic vision for a trilateral talk aims to create a second Yalta, carving up global spheres of influence.
Even if Xi and Trump are unlikely to agree to the arrangement, the image of the U.S., Russia and China jointly negotiating another country's fate would send a strong signal.
However, the summit also carries risks for Xi. Some insiders say Chinese officials worry the geopolitical side‑show could eclipse Beijing’s plan to use APEC to showcase its regional role.

Those sources note Xi is trying to balance continued support for Putin with maintaining China’s economic ties to Europe, and a three‑way talk could pull China deeper into the Ukraine war and provoke European backlash, as Europe already views Beijing’s tilt toward Moscow with suspicion.

items.title: 美烏矛盾與法國騷亂推升美元！歐元兌多數G10貨幣走貶 今早兌美元一度大跌0.5%
items.title_en: US-Ukraine Tensions and French Unrest Boost the Dollar! Euro Falls Against Most G10 Currencies, Briefly Dropping 0.5% Against the Dollar This Morning
paras: 受美烏矛盾進一步升高及法國大規模抗議活動影響，市場對歐元信心受挫，歐元兌多數G10貨幣在今(19)日亞洲早盤交易時段走低。
周末期間，法國多個城市抗議活動演變為警方與示威者之間的衝突，爆發法國多年來最嚴重的街頭暴力事件，出現搶劫、地標建築遭縱火情況。歐洲多國接連發生示威活動，法國的抗議規模最大，比利時、義大利、葡萄牙也受到波及。與此同時，烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基周日(18日)指責川普試圖向基輔施壓，逼迫烏克蘭向俄羅斯投降。
歐元兌美元在今日早盤一度貶值0.5%，最低貶至 1.1183 美元，隨後部分收復跌幅，交投於 1.1212 美元附近。受歐元走弱拖累，東歐貨幣表現弱於其他新興市場貨幣，美元兌波蘭茲羅提升值0.5%，報3.9071；美元兌匈牙利福林走升0.5%，報324.88，美元兌保加利亞列弗亦升值0.5%，報1.7485。
澳洲聯邦銀行外匯策略師Carol Kong表示：「市場恐將持續為歐元計入風險溢價。歐元兌美元本周可能測試 1.1130支撐價位，尤其是在地緣緊張進一步推高美元的情況下。」
paras_en: Rising US‑Ukraine tensions and large‑scale protests in France have dented market confidence in the euro, causing the euro to fall against most G10 currencies during Asian early‑trade on the 19th.

Over the weekend, protests in several French cities escalated into clashes between police and demonstrators, sparking the most severe street violence France has seen in years, including robberies and arson of landmark buildings. Demonstrations spread across multiple European countries, with France seeing the largest protests, and Belgium, Italy and Portugal also affected. At the same time, Ukrainian President Zelensky on Sunday (the 18th) accused former U.S. President Trump of trying to pressure Kyiv into surrendering to Russia.

The euro‑dollar pair slipped as much as 0.5% in early trade today, hitting a low of 1.1183 USD before partially regaining ground and trading around 1.1212 USD. The euro’s weakness also weighed on Eastern European currencies, which underperformed other emerging‑market currencies: the dollar rose 0.5% against the Polish zloty to 3.9071, against the Hungarian forint to 324.88, and against the Bulgarian lev to 1.7485.

Carol Kong, FX strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said: “The market is likely to continue pricing a risk premium into the euro. The euro‑dollar pair could test the 1.1130 support level this week, especially if geopolitical tensions further lift the dollar.”

items.title: 外資撤走逾千億億美元 韓股從AI贏家變重災區、散戶慘套
items.title_en: Foreign Investors Pull Out Over $100 Billion; Korean Stocks Shift from AI Winners to Disaster Zone, Retail Investors Suffer
paras: 韓國股市從AI行情的大贏家，轉為外資大舉撤出的重災區。南韓綜合指數(KOSPI) ）上半年一度漲逾一倍，下半年至今卻下跌40%，成交額較5月底高峰萎縮逾七成。隨著外資賣股、企業回購接近尾聲，追逐AI熱潮進場的投資人，正承受資金退潮的衝擊。
韓國確實受惠於AI產業蓬勃發展。三星電子(005930KS) 與SK海力士(000660KS) 位居記憶體、HBM及AI伺服器供應鏈核心，營收與獲利成長帶來實質經濟貢獻，估值又低於美國科技巨頭，成為全球資金布局AI的重要標的。
AI紅利推升股價 外資轉身撤離
在投行研究報告、ETF資金與衍生性商品槓桿推動下，記憶體股逐漸從傳統景氣循環股，被市場視為AI基礎設施成長股，帶動KOSPI上半年領漲全球主要股市。
然而，當估值與獲利預期持續攀升，企業繳出亮眼成績，也未必足以推動股價。前期積極買進的外資轉向獲利了結，曾經推升行情的資金，成為下半年賣壓的重要來源。
即使歷經修正，KOSPI自2025年以來累計漲幅仍超過130%。三星與SK海力士股價雖從高檔回落約一半，過去兩年市值漲幅仍分別超過三倍及6.4倍，凸顯不同進場時點的投資人，面臨截然不同的結果。
外資賣超集中兩大龍頭
截至10月14日，外資今年在韓國主要股票市場累計淨賣出約203.7兆韓元，其中三星與SK海力士合計約176兆韓元，占總賣超約86%。今年外資從韓國股市撤出約1,310億美元，規模居亞洲主要市場之首。
韓國對外資的依賴，也反映在持股結構。截至今年6月，外資持有韓股總市值比重約37.8%至38.9%，美國投資人約占外資持股的42%。
三星外資持股比率從8月初約46.70%，降至10月初的46.38%，為2008年以來最低；SK海力士則從50.84%降至49.59%，低於十年平均。
兩家公司合計占KOSPI權重超過一半，外資集中出售這兩檔股票，對指數形成明顯壓力。10月14日，韓國國民年金基金在國會聽證會上，甚至被批評是「外國投資者的提款機」，反映市場對外資撤離與本土資金承接賣壓的不滿。
回購將退場 散戶承接力轉弱
韓股面臨的另一項問題，是外資持續賣出之際，其他買盤也逐漸減弱。
7月股市重挫後，散戶進場意願降溫。融資餘額從6月高峰38.6兆韓元降至約33兆韓元，券商帳戶待投資存款也從接近140兆韓元，減少至約100兆韓元，顯示市場可動用資金縮水。
先前支撐行情的企業回購，同樣接近尾聲。三星與SK海力士合計約55兆韓元的回購計畫，貢獻了上月市場大部分買盤，但三星回購已於10月上旬基本完成，SK海力士也僅剩少量收尾。
當外資賣壓延續、回購逐步退場，散戶又縮減投入，市場便缺乏足夠承接力量。企業仍具產業優勢，並不代表股價能免於資金撤離的衝擊。
產業仍有優勢 市場結構卻脆弱
這波修正並不代表韓國AI半導體產業失去競爭力，而是暴露股市過度集中的風險。當指數高度依賴兩家公司、單一產業與外部資金，漲勢容易被放大，資金撤離時也缺少緩衝。
1997年亞洲金融危機期間，韓國財閥高負債擴張，金融體系依賴海外資金續借，國際資本撤出後，韓元與股市重挫，最終被迫接受國際貨幣基金（IMF）援助。
這次情況與當年不同，風險主要集中於市場結構：外資對核心股票價格具有高度影響力，散戶透過槓桿與ETF參與，企業回購則成為短期支撐。一旦資金流向改變，這些支撐便可能同步轉弱。
不過，將跌勢全數歸咎於外資，也忽略了資金配置的現實。下半年貨幣政策預期由寬鬆轉向緊縮，升息與無風險收益率走高，都促使投資人重新比較不同市場的報酬與估值，獲利了結也有其背景。
槓桿放大跌幅 高檔進場代價沉重
對高檔進場的投資人而言，槓桿進一步放大損失。在香港掛牌、曾受到追捧的兩倍做多SK海力士ETF，最新報價為19.22元，相較6月底高點193.65元，跌幅約91%。
韓股這輪大起大落顯示，產業成長與投資報酬並非必然同步。AI帶來的營收與獲利紅利仍在，但股價還取決於估值、資金流向與市場承接能力。
當外資撤離、回購減弱，最晚進場且使用高槓桿的投資人，往往承受最沉重的修正代價。
paras_en: Korean equities have shifted from being the big winners of the AI rally to a disaster zone as foreign investors pull out en masse. The KOSPI index, which surged more than double in the first half of the year, has fallen about 40% in the second half and trading volume has shrunk by over 70% from its late‑May peak. As foreign selling and corporate buybacks near their end, investors who chased the AI hype are now feeling the impact of a capital outflow.

South Korea has indeed benefited from the booming AI industry. Samsung Electronics (005930KS) and SK Hynix (000660KS) sit at the core of the memory, HBM and AI‑server supply chain, delivering real economic contribution through revenue and profit growth, and their valuations remain lower than those of U.S. tech giants, making them key targets for global AI capital allocation.
AI‑driven upside lifts stock prices, foreign investors turn away

Backed by investment‑bank research reports, ETF inflows and leveraged derivative products, memory stocks have gradually been re‑classified from traditional cyclical plays to AI‑infrastructure growth stocks, helping the KOSPI lead global major markets in the first half of the year.

However, as valuations and profit expectations kept climbing, even stellar corporate results were not enough to sustain price gains. Foreign investors who bought aggressively early are now taking profits, and the capital that once propelled the rally has become a major source of selling pressure in the second half.

Even after the correction, the KOSPI has risen more than 130% since 2025. Although Samsung and SK Hynix have each fallen roughly half from their peaks, their market caps have still more than tripled and increased 6.4‑fold respectively over the past two years, highlighting how investors who entered at different times face vastly different outcomes.
Foreign investors’ net selling is concentrated in two giants

As of Oct. 14, foreign investors have sold a net total of about KRW 203.7 trillion in Korea’s main equity market this year, with Samsung and SK Hynix accounting for roughly KRW 176 trillion, or about 86% of the total outflow. Foreign investors have withdrawn roughly $131 billion from Korean stocks this year, the largest pull‑back among Asian markets.

Korea’s reliance on foreign capital is also reflected in its ownership structure. By June this year, foreign investors held about 37.8%‑38.9% of the total market value of Korean equities, with U.S. investors accounting for roughly 42% of foreign holdings.
Foreign ownership of Samsung fell from about 46.70% in early August to 46.38% in early October, the lowest level since 2008; SK Hynix’s fell from 50.84% to 49.59%, below its ten‑year average.

The two companies together make up more than half of the KOSPI’s weighting, so foreign investors’ concentrated selling of these stocks puts clear pressure on the index. On Oct. 14, the Korean National Pension Service was even criticized in a parliamentary hearing as a “cash‑cow for foreign investors,” reflecting market frustration over foreign exits and domestic capital’s limited ability to absorb the selling.
Buybacks are winding down and retail buying power is weakening
Another issue for Korean stocks is that as foreign investors keep selling, other buying pressure is also fading.

After the market plunge in July, retail enthusiasm cooled. Margin balances fell from a June peak of KRW 38.6 trillion to about KRW 33 trillion, and broker‑account cash earmarked for investment dropped from nearly KRW 140 trillion to roughly KRW 100 trillion, indicating a shrinkage in deployable capital.

Corporate buybacks that had previously supported the rally are also nearing completion. Samsung and SK Hynix together have a KRW 55 trillion buyback program that supplied most of last month’s buying, but Samsung’s repurchase was essentially finished in early October and SK Hynix has only a small tail left.

When foreign selling persists, buybacks retreat, and retail investors cut back, the market lacks sufficient support. The companies still have industry advantages, but that does not shield their share prices from the impact of capital outflows.
Industry strengths remain but market structure is fragile

This correction does not mean Korea’s AI semiconductor sector has lost its competitiveness; rather, it exposes the risk of an overly concentrated market. When an index is heavily dependent on two firms, a single industry and foreign capital, gains can be amplified and withdrawals leave little buffer.

During the 1997 Asian financial crisis, Korean chaebols expanded with high debt and the financial system relied on overseas funding. When international capital fled, the won and the stock market crashed, eventually forcing Korea to accept IMF assistance.

The current situation differs from 1997; the risk now lies mainly in market structure: foreign investors wield outsized influence over core stock prices, retail investors participate via leverage and ETFs, and corporate buybacks act as short‑term support. If capital flows shift, those supports can weaken simultaneously.

Nevertheless, blaming the entire decline on foreign investors ignores the realities of fund allocation. In the second half of the year, monetary policy expectations are shifting from easing to tightening, with higher rates and risk‑free yields prompting investors to reassess returns and valuations across markets, making profit‑taking understandable.
Leverage magnifies losses; buying at highs is costly

For investors who entered at lofty levels, leverage further amplifies losses. The SK Hynix double‑long ETF listed in Hong Kong, once hotly chased, now trades at 19.22 HKD, down from its late‑June high of 193.65 HKD – a drop of about 91%.

This roller‑coaster in Korean stocks shows that industry growth and investment returns do not automatically move together. AI‑driven revenue and profit upside remain, but share prices still depend on valuations, capital flows and market‑absorption capacity.
When foreign investors exit and buybacks weaken, the latest entrants who used high leverage tend to bear the heaviest correction costs.

items.title: 美烏矛盾持續升級！澤倫斯基控美施壓「投降」後提新條件：停打俄煉油廠換「愛國者」飛彈
items.title_en: US‑Ukraine Rift Escalates: Zelensky Accuses Washington of Pressuring Ukraine to ‘Surrender’ and Offers New Terms – Halt Attacks on Russian Refineries in Exchange for Patriot Missiles
paras: 烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基週日(18日)接受《彭博資訊》訪問時指控，美國正透過軍援、衛星通信與能源政策向基輔施壓，試圖迫使烏國接受對俄有利的停戰條件，但他也強調並非斷言華府以此為目標，但近期一連串動作「看起來如此」，雙方持續一週的公開爭執進一步升級。
爭議核心從烏軍打擊俄國煉油廠，外溢至對俄制裁、星鏈與軍用星盾服務、情資共享及愛國者飛彈供應。澤倫斯基提出交換方案：烏方停止攻擊俄柴油供應鏈，美國則增供愛國者攔截彈保護能源設施與城市，但華府目前僅要求烏國停手，未接受交換。
華府立場為壓低能源價格、維持與莫斯科談判渠道，稱與俄柴油供應安排是避免「把普丁趕出談判桌」，並反指澤倫斯基拖延戰事。
基輔的立場則認為，俄軍持續轟炸烏國能源設施之際，華府卻減輕俄經濟壓力，只會削弱逼俄收手動能。
星鏈與情資爭議加劇。澤倫斯基稱烏國境內設備時速逾161公里後服務受限，矛頭指向白宮，華府否認下達指令。此外，澤倫斯基證實美一度暫停預警俄彈道飛彈來襲的共享機制，之後恢復。
與此同時，愛國者交付也成摩擦點：澤倫斯基說烏國已付款部分卻被延遲，目前月供約12枚，僅拜登時期四分之一，問題在政治決定而非產能。川普日前簽行政令暫緩實施部分對俄制裁，配合美俄柴油協議，澤倫斯基批此舉錯誤。
當前戰場壓力驟增。俄軍入冬前加大打擊烏國電力設施，多城長時間停電；烏攔截彈有限，星鏈、情資與愛國者任一環鬆動，都直接影響防空能力。澤倫斯基警告風險已逼近海嘯級，但華府優先順序顯已從「撐烏」部分轉向「壓油價、控盤、保談判」。
paras_en: In a Bloomberg interview on Sunday, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky accused the United States of using military aid, satellite communications and energy policy to pressure Kyiv into accepting a cease‑fire that would favor Russia. He stressed he is not claiming this is Washington’s explicit goal, but recent actions “look that way,” and a week‑long public dispute between the two sides has further intensified.

The controversy stems from Ukraine’s strikes on Russian oil refineries and has spilled over into broader issues such as sanctions on Russia, the use of Starlink and military‑grade Starshield services, intelligence sharing, and the supply of Patriot missiles. Zelensky put forward a swap: Ukraine would stop hitting Russia’s diesel‑supply chain, and the United States would increase Patriot interceptors to protect energy facilities and cities. So far, Washington has only demanded that Ukraine cease its attacks and has not accepted the proposed exchange.

The U.S. position is aimed at lowering energy prices and preserving a negotiation channel with Moscow, saying that keeping a Russian diesel‑supply arrangement helps avoid “pushing Putin off the negotiating table,” and it has accused Zelensky of dragging out the war.

Kyiv’s view is that while Russian forces continue to bomb Ukrainian energy infrastructure, the United States is easing economic pressure on Russia, which only weakens the leverage to force Moscow to back down.

The Starlink and intelligence dispute has intensified. Zelensky said that once equipment inside Ukraine exceeded speeds of 161 km/h, service was throttled, pointing the finger at the White House, which denied issuing any such order. He also confirmed that the United States briefly halted the sharing of early‑warning data on Russian ballistic missile launches before restoring it.

At the same time, Patriot deliveries have become another flashpoint: Zelensky said Ukraine has paid for a portion of the missiles but deliveries have been delayed, with the current monthly supply at about 12 units—only a quarter of the rate under the Biden administration. He blamed political decisions rather than production capacity. Former President Trump recently signed an executive order to pause parts of the sanctions regime against Russia, aligning with the U.S.–Russia diesel agreement, a move Zelensky condemned as a mistake.

The pressure on the battlefield has surged. In the run‑up to winter, Russian forces have stepped up attacks on Ukraine’s power grid, causing prolonged blackouts in multiple cities. Ukraine’s interceptor stockpiles are limited, and any slack in Starlink, intelligence or Patriot coverage directly erodes its air‑defence capability. Zelensky warned that the risk is approaching a “tsunami‑level” threat, but the U.S. appears to have shifted its priority from “supporting Ukraine” to “pressuring oil prices, controlling the market, and safeguarding negotiations.”

items.title: 賣出訊號解除！美銀Hartnett看11月中旬重返科技股 關鍵在晶片價格
items.title_en: Sell‑Signal Lifted! BofA’s Hartnett Sees Mid‑November Return to Tech Stocks, Chip Prices Key
paras: 美銀證券策略師Michael Hartnett指出，美銀牛熊指標已跌破警戒門檻，結束先前的賣出訊號，但尚未發出買進訊號。投資人能否在11月中旬重返科技股，關鍵在於晶片價格能否延續漲勢；若價格回落，恐意味AI融資環境進一步收緊、資本支出成長見頂。
Hartnett在最新一期《Flow Show》報告中指出，美銀牛熊指標由8.1降至7.4，跌破8.0門檻，正式結束5月26日觸發的賣出訊號。舊版指標也從5.6降至5.1，兩者均顯示，夏季極度樂觀的市場情緒已告終。
賣出訊號結束 買點仍待確認
指標下滑，主要受到全球股市上漲廣度惡化、避險基金持有原油與標普500期貨空單、黃金期貨多單減少，以及高收益債和新興市場債資金流入轉弱影響。科技股持續吸金，則是唯一推升指標的因素。
不過，賣出訊號終止不代表買點已到。美銀廣度規則顯示，全球股市指數淨超賣比例達52%，為2025年4月以來最高，但仍低於觸發反向買進訊號所需的88%。
Hartnett認為，除非目前仍處於超買狀態的美國、台灣與巴西股市再跌6%至10%，否則短期內難以達到這項門檻。
科技股重挫，資金仍未明顯撤離
儘管那斯達克100指數單週跌幅近6%，資金流向卻未顯示投資人大舉撤出。EPFR截至當週三的數據顯示，股票基金淨流入644億美元，債券基金吸金118億美元，現金則流出531億美元。
美銀私人客戶的股票配置占比達66.4%，創歷史新高，現金占比則降至歷史低點9.3%。今年全球股票基金淨流入金額換算成年率達1.3兆美元，其中科技基金達1960億美元，超過先前紀錄的2.5倍。
美銀10月基金經理人調查也顯示，科技股超配程度為2020年8月以來最高，反映市場情緒雖降溫，投資部位仍高度集中。
韓股的落差尤其明顯。南韓綜合指數(KOSPI) 指數自6月高點下跌30%，但8月資金流入高峰過後，每流入100美元，僅有7美元撤離。
Hartnett指出，外資是當週賣壓主力，加上股票回購窗口接近關閉，真正的撤資可能尚未開始。
AI融資壓力升高，暫守防禦立場
Hartnett目前仍採取防禦策略，並列出重新擁抱風險資產的兩項前提，包括聯準會10月28日升息以恢復信譽，以及AI融資疑慮緩解，但兩者目前均未實現。
市場預期聯準會10月升息的機率，已由逾50%降至14%；AI信貸市場則剛經歷今年最差的一週。CoreWeave債券跌入困境區間，5年期信用違約交換（CDS）利差隱含的五年違約機率約63%。
高盛數據顯示，CoreWeave於2031年到期的債券，與美國公債的利差一度超過1100個基點。甲骨文5年期CDS也急升，但整體投資級科技債利差幾乎未動，顯示高槓桿借款人承受的壓力最大。
此外，美國10年期實質殖利率逼近3%，過去這一水準曾與網路泡沫破裂、全球金融危機及矽谷銀行事件等風險事件相伴出現，也讓Hartnett維持審慎態度。
11月能否回補科技股 晶片價格是關鍵
Hartnett認為，半導體價格將是左右2027年經濟與市場走向的重要變數。高盛數據顯示，半導體生產者物價指數在經歷近30年下行後，近期急劇攀升。
若晶片價格持續上漲，意味美中AI競賽延續，也有助維持市場對美國政府隱性支撐股債價格的預期。在這種情境下，投資人將於11月中旬重返科技股，並在邁入2027年之際，反轉「放空科技股、做多債券」的部位。
反之，若晶片價格回落，可能代表AI信貸進一步收緊、資本支出成長見頂，支撐名目GDP繁榮的動力也將動搖。屆時債券表現可能較佳，仰賴AI資本支出題材支撐估值的資產則將承壓，2027年報酬來源也可能從資本增值轉向收益。
市場共識預估，超大規模雲端業者資本支出將由2026年的8070億美元，增至2027年的1.16兆美元；自由現金流則預計由今年負630億美元，惡化至明年負1630億美元，凸顯融資環境的重要性。
暫不加碼科技股 布局殖利率見頂受惠資產
在操作上，Hartnett暫不加碼科技股，而是增加可能受惠於殖利率見頂的資產，包括小型股、不動產投資信託（REITs）及非必需消費類股。後者在美銀10月調查中的低配程度，為2008年7月以來最高。
長期配置方面，他維持超配黃金、大宗商品與新興市場，但認為應逐步縮減長期放空債券及低配中國的部位。
Hartnett也指出，標普500指數已有355檔成分股較52週高點下跌逾10%，其中188檔跌逾20%、93檔跌逾30%。指數表面之下，個股已承受相當程度的修正，可能為耐心等待布局時機的投資人帶來價值空間。
paras_en: BofA Securities strategist Michael Hartnett said the bank’s bull‑bear indicator has fallen below the warning threshold, ending the previous sell‑signal, but a buy‑signal has not yet been issued. Whether investors can return to tech stocks by mid‑November hinges on whether chip prices can keep rising; a price pull‑back could signal tighter AI financing and a peak in cap‑ex growth.

In the latest “Flow Show” report Hartnett noted the bull‑bear indicator dropped from 8.1 to 7.4, slipping below the 8.0 mark and formally ending the sell‑signal triggered on May 26. The older version of the indicator also fell from 5.6 to 5.1, both showing that the extreme optimism of the summer market mood is over.
Sell‑signal ended, buy‑point still unconfirmed

The indicator’s decline is mainly due to a worsening breadth in global equity markets, hedge funds holding short positions in oil and S&P 500 futures, a reduction in long gold futures, and weaker inflows into high‑yield and emerging‑market debt. Continued inflows into tech stocks are the only factor that still lifts the indicator.

However, the end of the sell‑signal does not mean a buying opportunity has arrived. BofA’s breadth rule shows the net oversold ratio of global equity indices is 52%, the highest since April 2025, but still below the 88% needed to trigger a reverse‑buy signal.
Hartnett believes that unless the currently overbought U.S., Taiwan and Brazil markets fall another 6‑10%, the threshold is unlikely to be met in the short term.
Tech stocks tumble, but capital has not clearly fled

Even though the Nasdaq‑100 fell almost 6% over the week, fund flows did not show a massive investor exodus. EPFR data through Wednesday showed a net inflow of $64.4 billion into equity funds, $11.8 billion into bond funds, and a net outflow of $53.1 billion from cash.

BofA’s private‑client equity allocation reached 66.4%, a historic high, while cash holdings fell to a historic low of 9.3%. Global equity fund net inflows this year amount to an annualised $1.3 trillion, with tech funds alone attracting $196 billion – more than 2.5 times the previous record.
A BofA October survey of fund managers also showed tech‑stock over‑weighting at its highest since August 2020, indicating that despite cooler sentiment, positions remain heavily concentrated.
The gap is especially stark in South Korea. The KOSPI has slid 30% from its June peak, yet after the August inflow peak, every $100 that came in only saw $7 withdrawn.
Hartnett said foreign investors were the main sellers that week, and with the stock‑repurchase window nearing its end, true capital outflows may not have started yet.
AI financing pressure rises, staying defensive for now

Hartnett remains defensive and lists two pre‑conditions for re‑embracing risk assets: a rate hike by the Fed on Oct. 28 to restore credibility, and a easing of AI‑financing concerns – neither of which has materialised yet.

The market’s probability view of an October Fed hike has dropped from over 50% to 14%; the AI credit market just endured its worst week of the year. CoreWeave bonds fell into distress, with the five‑year CDS spread implying a roughly 63% five‑year default probability.

Goldman data show CoreWeave’s 2031 bond spread over U.S. Treasuries once exceeded 11,100 bps. Oracle’s five‑year CDS also spiked, but overall investment‑grade tech‑bond spreads barely moved, indicating that highly‑leveraged borrowers feel the most pressure.

In addition, the real yield on the U.S. 10‑year Treasury is approaching 3%. Historically, that level has coincided with the dot‑com bust, the global financial crisis and the Silicon Valley Bank collapse, prompting Hartnett to stay cautious.
Can chip prices decide a November tech‑stock rebound?

Hartnett believes semiconductor prices will be a decisive factor for the 2027 economic and market outlook. Goldman data show the semiconductor producer price index, after nearly three decades of decline, has recently surged sharply.

If chip prices keep rising, it suggests the U.S.–China AI race continues and helps sustain market expectations of implicit U.S. government support for equity‑bond prices. In that scenario investors would return to tech stocks by mid‑November and, heading into 2027, reverse the “short tech, long bonds” stance.

Conversely, a chip‑price decline could signal tighter AI credit, a cap‑ex peak and a weakening of the drivers behind nominal‑GDP growth. Bonds would likely outperform, while assets that rely on AI‑cap‑ex‑driven valuations would feel pressure, shifting 2027 returns from capital gains to income.

Consensus forecasts estimate that ultra‑large cloud providers’ cap‑ex will rise from $807 billion in 2026 to $1.16 trillion in 2027; free cash flow is projected to worsen from a $63 billion deficit this year to a $163 billion deficit next year, underscoring the importance of financing conditions.
Hold off on adding to tech, favour assets that benefit from a yield‑peak environment

In practice Hartnett is not adding to tech positions now, but is increasing exposure to assets that could benefit from a yield‑peak, such as small‑caps, REITs and consumer‑discretionary stocks. The latter’s under‑weighting in BofA’s October survey is at its highest since July 2008.
For the long run he remains over‑weight in gold, commodities and emerging markets, while recommending a gradual reduction of long‑bond shorts and a low‑weight stance on China.

Hartnett also noted that 355 S&P 500 constituents have fallen more than 10% from their 52‑week highs, with 188 down over 20% and 93 down over 30%. Beneath the index’s surface, individual stocks have endured sizable corrections, potentially offering value opportunities for patient investors waiting to deploy capital.

items.title: 馬斯克秀飛行汽車 大西洋月刊潑冷水「永遠不該造出來」
items.title_en: Musk Shows Flying Car; Atlantic Monthly Douses It With Cold Water, Saying It Should ‘Never Have Been Built’
paras: 《大西洋月刊》評論指出，飛行汽車或許永遠不該被造出來，因為這個延續百年的夢想，作為幻想比化為現實更有吸引力。
特斯拉(TSLA-US) 上周展示特斯拉 Roadster「飛行」原型車，雖然空中特技令人驚豔，卻也凸顯了核心問題：人們追求的究竟是能飛的汽車，還是擺脫道路束縛、永遠被推遲的自由想像？
這輛跑車倒掛在弧形軌道上，利用與 SpaceX(SPCX-US) 合作設計的空氣動力推進器，上演一連串空中特技，包括飛躍一輛特斯拉 Semi 卡車。
展示結束後，馬斯克引用前 PayPal 合夥人提爾（Peter Thiel）的名言：「我們想要的是飛行汽車，結果得到的卻是140個字元。」
這句話出自提爾旗下創投公司 Founders Fund 於2011年發表的科技宣言，批評全球智慧與資金未投入重大挑戰，反而流向推特等社群平台。
這番說法有個矛盾：Founders Fund 當時最重要的投資，正是同屬社群平台的 Facebook。更根本的問題則是，人們真的想要一輛飛行汽車嗎？如同噴射背包，飛行汽車象徵的可能不只是未來，而是透過科技突破實現個人自由。
百年嘗試 始終難以普及
從字面意義來看，飛行汽車並非新鮮夢想。早期實用飛機同樣先在地面滑行，再升空飛行，某種程度上就是長了翅膀的汽車。
1917年，柯蒂斯（Glenn Curtiss）打造配備可拆卸機翼與螺旋槳的 Curtiss Autoplane，卻未能真正有效飛行。沃特曼（Waldo Waterman）1937年的 Arrowbile 在飛行方面更成功，但不具商業可行性。後來的 Taylor Aerocar 雖於1956年取得聯邦政府認證，也始終未能量產。
後續嘗試同樣困難重重。1973年，斯莫林斯基（Henry Smolinski）將塞斯納飛機機翼裝上福特 Pinto，打造 AVE Mizar，卻在試飛事故中喪生。
莫勒（Paul Moller）從1960年代起多次開發可垂直起降的 Skycar，直到公司於2010年代中期陷入停滯。Terrafugia 的 Transition 則長年停留在「再過幾年就上市」的承諾，直到公司於2021年倒閉。
如今，馬斯克也提出時間表，宣稱 Roadster 將在2028年投產，還補上一句「說真的」。
飛越道路 成為自由象徵
評論認為，要理解飛行汽車為何令人著迷，必須回到汽車普及後的社會變化。當汽車在美國成為主流，取代火車與電車等集體交通工具，它也逐漸象徵個人自主權，讓人能獨自前往想去的地方。
然而，這份自由始終受制於道路。即使美國擁有廣闊土地與綿延公路，道路似乎永遠不夠，於是從上方飛越，成了擺脫限制的想像。
早在1923年，科幻先驅根斯巴克（Hugo Gernsback）便構想以陀螺儀驅動的 Helicar，希望將旅客從紐約壅塞街道解放出來。1927年的電影《大都會》讓小型飛行器穿梭城市上空；1962年的動畫《傑森一家》，則進一步將飛行汽車描繪成人人使用的通勤工具。
這些作品承載的共同願望，是當地面生活愈來愈擁擠，天空便成為新自由的寄託。
能短暫離地 不代表能飛行通勤
不過，Roadster 與這些真實或虛構的前輩並不相同。它的空氣風扇系統，主要作用似乎是提高車輪抓地力，搭配車尾火箭推進器，使車輛在展示中從靜止加速至時速60英里，耗時不到一秒。
至於所謂的飛行，更接近桶滾、原地跳躍等空中特技。車輛確實能短暫離地，但是否具備、或打算提供日常旅行與通勤所需的飛行能力，仍不清楚。
為避免造成人員傷亡，這場展示採無人駕駛方式進行。評論作者表示，眼前景象讓他想到的，是富有的機械愛好者在住宅區跳躍、旋轉而製造混亂，而非上班族搭乘飛行汽車往返職場。
真正吸引人的 是尚未實現的夢
任何從道路進入空域的車輛，都面臨龐大監管障礙，但評論認為，法規並非飛行汽車夢想遲遲未能實現的主要原因。更深層的問題是，這個夢想留在幻想中，或許比成為現實更有吸引力。
當汽車帶來的個人自由普及，道路也隨之擠滿奔波的人群，原本象徵自由的公路便成為另一種束縛，上方藍天則再次被賦予逃離現實的希望。即使是提爾口中的飛行汽車，也更像值得追求的象徵，而非真正值得落實的生活方式。
評論最後指出，Roadster 至少在這場展示中展現驚人能力，但它實現百年飛行汽車雄心的方式，是成為特技駕駛的載具，而非一般駕駛的飛行器。它最終滿足的，或許是馬斯克自己的夢想：宣稱交付了前人一個世紀以來都未能交付的事物。
paras_en: The Atlantic Monthly editorial argues that flying cars may never ought to be built, because this century‑old dream is more alluring as a fantasy than as a reality.

Tesla (TSLA‑US) displayed a “flying” prototype of the Roadster last week; while the aerial stunts were impressive, they also highlighted a core question: are people really after a car that can fly, or the freedom of shedding road constraints that has been perpetually postponed?

The sports car was inverted on a curved track and, using an aerodynamic thruster designed in partnership with SpaceX (SPCX‑US), performed a series of aerial maneuvers, including leaping over a Tesla Semi truck.
After the demonstration, Musk quoted former PayPal partner Peter Thiel: “What we wanted was a flying car, and what we got was 140 characters.”

The line comes from a 2011 technology manifesto issued by Thiel’s venture firm Founders Fund, which criticized the global brain‑power and capital being funneled into social platforms like Twitter rather than into major challenges.

The remark is contradictory because Founders Fund’s biggest investment at the time was in another social platform, Facebook. More fundamentally, the piece asks whether people truly want a flying car, or whether, like a jetpack, it symbolizes personal liberty achieved through technological breakthroughs.
A Century‑Long Quest That Has Never Gone Mainstream
Literally, the flying‑car idea is not new. Early practical airplanes also taxied on the ground before taking off, essentially cars with wings.

In 1917 Glenn Curtiss built the Curtiss Autoplane with detachable wings and a propeller, but it never achieved effective flight. Waldo Waterman’s 1937 Arrowbile was more successful in the air but commercially unviable. Later, the Taylor Aerocar earned federal certification in 1956 yet never entered mass production.
Subsequent attempts ran into similar hurdles. In 1973 Henry Smolinski attached Cessna wings to a Ford Pinto to create the AVE Mizar, but the test‑flight ended in a fatal crash.

Paul Moller pursued vertical‑takeoff Skycars from the 1960s until his company stalled in the mid‑2010s. Terrafugia’s Transition lingered for years on promises of a “launch in a few years” before the firm folded in 2021.
Now Musk has set a timetable, claiming the Roadster will go into production in 2028, adding a casual “seriously.”
Flying Over Roads as a Symbol of Freedom

Commentators say that to understand the allure of flying cars one must look back at the social changes after automobiles became ubiquitous. When cars displaced trains and streetcars in the United States, they also came to represent personal autonomy, letting individuals travel wherever they wished.

Yet that freedom remained bounded by roads. Even with America’s vast land and endless highways, the road network always seemed insufficient, prompting the fantasy of soaring above to escape those limits.

As early as 1923, sci‑fi pioneer Hugo Gernsback imagined a gyroscope‑driven Helicar to free passengers from congested New York streets. The 1927 film “Metropolis” showed tiny aircraft zipping over a city, and the 1962 cartoon “The Jetsons” portrayed flying cars as everyday commuter vehicles.
These works share a common wish: as ground‑level life grew more crowded, the sky became a new repository for liberty.
Briefly Leaving the Ground Does Not Equal Commuter‑Ready Flight

However, the Roadster differs from these real or fictional predecessors. Its air‑fan system appears mainly to boost wheel traction, while a rear‑mounted rocket provides thrust that accelerated the vehicle from a standstill to 60 mph in under a second during the demo.

The so‑called “flight” was more akin to barrel rolls and hops in place. The car can lift off momentarily, but whether it possesses—or intends to provide—the sustained flight capability needed for everyday travel remains unclear.

To avoid injuries, the demonstration was conducted unmanned. The author of the commentary likened the spectacle to wealthy gadget enthusiasts jumping and spinning in residential neighborhoods, creating chaos, rather than to commuters using a flying car to get to work.
What Truly Captivates Is the Unfulfilled Dream

Any vehicle that moves from road to air faces massive regulatory hurdles, but the commentary argues that regulation is not the primary reason the flying‑car dream has stalled. A deeper issue is that the fantasy may be more attractive than turning it into reality.

When personal freedom spread through automobiles, roads became crowded with commuters, turning the once‑symbolic highways into another form of constraint, while the blue sky above regained its role as an imagined escape. Even the flying‑car Thiel mentions feels more like a coveted symbol than a practical lifestyle.

The commentary concludes that the Roadster demonstrated astonishing capabilities in this showcase, but its path to fulfilling a century‑old flying‑car ambition is as a stunt platform rather than a conventional aerial vehicle. Ultimately, it may satisfy Musk’s own dream: claiming to have delivered something no one has been able to deliver for a hundred years.

items.title: 蘋果CEO喊記憶體危機、「所有選項都考慮」 外界解讀中國貨成備選
items.title_en: Apple CEO Warns of Memory Crisis, Says "All Options Being Considered"; Analysts See China‑Made Chips as Possible Backup
paras: 蘋果(AAPL-US) 新任執行長特努斯（John Ternus）再度強調，記憶體供應受限已構成嚴重危機，蘋果必須考慮所有選項。儘管他未直接點名中國供應商，外界分析認為，中國製記憶體也可能成為替代方案，但是否採用仍未定案，且面臨美國政界阻力。
特努斯在美國《時代》雜誌當地時間15日公布的專訪中表示：「記憶體供應限制顯然是一場嚴重危機，我們的基本立場是必須考慮所有選項。」
特努斯於9月1日接替庫克出任蘋果執行長，上任後將供應鏈問題列為核心待解議題，背後原因是AI資料中心投資熱潮正改變記憶體市場的供需結構。
隨著半導體業者將產能集中於高頻寬記憶體（HBM）等AI產品，智慧型手機與個人電腦使用的一般記憶體也出現供應不足、價格大漲的情況，蘋果因此面臨供貨與成本雙重壓力。
據業界消息，今年第一季，三星電子(005930KS) 與SK海力士(000660KS) 供應給iPhone的低功耗DRAM價格，分別較前一季上漲80%與100%。《華爾街日報》指出，蘋果每年採購記憶體與儲存設備的金額達數百億美元。
為因應供應壓力，蘋果據傳已開始測試中國製記憶體。英國《金融時報》7月報導，蘋果正在測試長鑫科技(688825-CN) 的DRAM，並考慮優先用於在中國銷售的裝置。
《華爾街日報》8月也報導，蘋果正針對iPhone、MacBook等多條產品線測試長鑫記憶體，但尚未敲定是否採用，也未確定量產採購合約。
不過，採用中國供應商產品面臨政治阻力。美國參議院民主黨領袖舒默（Chuck Schumer）等7名跨黨派參議員，7月時曾致函蘋果，要求承諾不使用長鑫存儲與長江存儲（YMTC）的產品，理由是兩家公司被美國國防部列入中國軍事企業清單，存在國家安全疑慮。
特努斯表示，他已與川普政府官員會面，並討論這項議題。
外界觀察認為，若蘋果最終採用中國製記憶體，可能改變三星電子、SK海力士與美光等既有供應商的議價能力，並牽動全球記憶體供應鏈布局。
paras_en: Apple (AAPL-US) new chief executive John Ternus reiterated that constrained memory supply has become a serious crisis and Apple must consider every option. Although he did not name Chinese suppliers directly, analysts say Chinese‑made memory could be an alternative, but its adoption is not decided and faces resistance from U.S. policymakers.

In a interview with the U.S. edition of Time magazine published on the 15th local time, Ternus said, "The memory supply limitation is clearly a serious crisis, and our basic stance is that we must consider all options."

Ternus succeeded Tim Cook as Apple CEO on September 1, and has made supply‑chain issues a core priority, citing the AI data‑center investment boom that is reshaping memory market supply‑demand dynamics.

As semiconductor firms shift capacity toward high‑bandwidth memory (HBM) and other AI products, ordinary memory used in smartphones and PCs is becoming scarce and prices are soaring, putting Apple under dual pressure of supply shortages and higher costs.

Industry sources say that in the first quarter of this year Samsung Electronics (005930KS) and SK Hynix (000660KS) raised the price of low‑power DRAM supplied to iPhone by 80% and 100% respectively compared with the previous quarter. The Wall Street Journal noted that Apple spends several tens of billions of dollars each year on memory and storage devices.

To cope with the supply squeeze, Apple is reportedly already testing Chinese‑made memory. The Financial Times reported in July that Apple is testing DRAM from ChangXin Technology (688825-CN) and is considering prioritising it for devices sold in China.

The Wall Street Journal also reported in August that Apple is testing ChangXin memory across multiple product lines such as iPhone and MacBook, but has not yet decided whether to adopt it nor finalized any mass‑production purchase contracts.

However, using products from Chinese suppliers faces political pushback. In July, Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and six other bipartisan senators sent a letter to Apple demanding a commitment not to use memory from ChangXin and Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC), citing that both firms are on the U.S. Department of Defense’s list of Chinese military companies and pose national‑security concerns.
Ternus said he has met with officials from the Trump administration and discussed the issue.

Observers note that if Apple ultimately adopts Chinese‑made memory, it could shift bargaining power away from existing suppliers such as Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron and reshape the global memory‑supply chain layout.

paras: 伊朗最高國家安全委員會秘書雷札伊周日(18日)警告，已針對美國與以色列「任何新的冒險行徑」擬定回應方案，並稱伊朗武裝力量的反制將比先前「12天戰爭」與「40天戰爭」更具毀滅性，「新作戰計畫不會遵循他們熟悉的規則」。
雷札伊身分相當具分量，曾任革命衛隊總司令，現掌伊朗安全決策核心機構。這一表態正值中東海域風險上升，因根據英國海上貿易行動辦公室數據，沙烏地阿拉伯朱拜勒附近海域接連有油輪遭不明發射物及火箭彈襲擊，阿曼灣、荷姆茲海峽週邊亦傳船舶受襲，船員暫報安全。
華府則同步釋放矛盾訊號。川普上周受訪時表示，不打算對伊朗使用核武器，也不預見部署美軍地面部隊，但華府仍保留常規打擊選項。
伊朗外長阿拉格齊則回應，德黑蘭不會在壓力下放棄主權權利，但仍準備對話。
分析人士認為，伊朗意在以強硬威懾換取談判籌碼，商船遇襲與荷姆茲通航風險則持續牽動能源市場神經。
paras_en: Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary, Rezaei, warned on Sunday (the 18th) that a response plan has been drafted for any new adventurism by the United States and Israel, and said Iran’s armed forces would retaliate with a level of devastation greater than the previous “12‑day war” and “40‑day war,” noting that the new operational plan would not follow the rules they are accustomed to.

Rezaei’s statement carries weight; he is a former commander of the Revolutionary Guard and now heads Iran’s core security‑decision body. The remark comes as risks in Middle‑East waters rise, with UK Maritime Trade Operations data showing a series of attacks on tankers near Saudi Arabia’s Jabal al‑Dukhan, as well as incidents in the Oman Sea and the Strait of Hormuz where vessels were struck by unknown projectiles and rockets, though crews have so far reported being safe.

Washington simultaneously sent mixed signals. In an interview last week, President Trump said he does not intend to use nuclear weapons against Iran and does not foresee deploying U.S. ground troops, yet the administration still retains the option of conventional strikes.
Iranian Foreign Minister Amir‑Abdollahian responded that Tehran will not relinquish its sovereign rights under pressure, but remains ready for dialogue.

Analysts believe Iran is using a hard‑line deterrent to gain bargaining chips in negotiations, and the ongoing attacks on commercial vessels and the navigation risk in the Strait of Hormuz continue to nerve the energy markets.

items.title: 美烏矛盾與法國騷亂推升美元！歐元兌多數G10貨幣走貶 今早兌美元一度大跌0.5%
items.title_en: US-Ukraine Tensions and French Unrest Boost the Dollar! Euro Falls Against Most G10 Currencies, Briefly Dropping 0.5% Against the Dollar This Morning
paras: 受美烏矛盾進一步升高及法國大規模抗議活動影響，市場對歐元信心受挫，歐元兌多數G10貨幣在今(19)日亞洲早盤交易時段走低。
周末期間，法國多個城市抗議活動演變為警方與示威者之間的衝突，爆發法國多年來最嚴重的街頭暴力事件，出現搶劫、地標建築遭縱火情況。歐洲多國接連發生示威活動，法國的抗議規模最大，比利時、義大利、葡萄牙也受到波及。與此同時，烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基周日(18日)指責川普試圖向基輔施壓，逼迫烏克蘭向俄羅斯投降。
歐元兌美元在今日早盤一度貶值0.5%，最低貶至 1.1183 美元，隨後部分收復跌幅，交投於 1.1212 美元附近。受歐元走弱拖累，東歐貨幣表現弱於其他新興市場貨幣，美元兌波蘭茲羅提升值0.5%，報3.9071；美元兌匈牙利福林走升0.5%，報324.88，美元兌保加利亞列弗亦升值0.5%，報1.7485。
澳洲聯邦銀行外匯策略師Carol Kong表示：「市場恐將持續為歐元計入風險溢價。歐元兌美元本周可能測試 1.1130支撐價位，尤其是在地緣緊張進一步推高美元的情況下。」
paras_en: Rising US‑Ukraine tensions and large‑scale protests in France have dented market confidence in the euro, causing the euro to fall against most G10 currencies during Asian early‑trade on the 19th.

Over the weekend, protests in several French cities escalated into clashes between police and demonstrators, sparking the most severe street violence France has seen in years, including robberies and arson of landmark buildings. Demonstrations spread across multiple European countries, with France seeing the largest protests, and Belgium, Italy and Portugal also affected. At the same time, Ukrainian President Zelensky on Sunday (the 18th) accused former U.S. President Trump of trying to pressure Kyiv into surrendering to Russia.

The euro‑dollar pair slipped as much as 0.5% in early trade today, hitting a low of 1.1183 USD before partially regaining ground and trading around 1.1212 USD. The euro’s weakness also weighed on Eastern European currencies, which underperformed other emerging‑market currencies: the dollar rose 0.5% against the Polish zloty to 3.9071, against the Hungarian forint to 324.88, and against the Bulgarian lev to 1.7485.

Carol Kong, FX strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said: “The market is likely to continue pricing a risk premium into the euro. The euro‑dollar pair could test the 1.1130 support level this week, especially if geopolitical tensions further lift the dollar.”

items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉美元逾1個月來首見單週跌幅 升息預期降溫、AI疑慮持續
items.title_en: <New York Forex> US Dollar Records First Weekly Decline in Over a Month as Rate‑Hike Expectations Cool and AI Concerns Persist
paras: 美元周五(16日)走低，兌歐元與日元均創下逾1個月來首見單週貶值，反映市場對聯準會(Fed)升息的預期降溫，以及投資人對AI引發股市賣壓的疑慮持續存在。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌0.17%，報101.87，本週下跌約0.35%。
本週公布的消費者物價與生產者物價數據均高於預期，一度令市場感到不安。不過，聯準會官員的談話顯示，目前沒有急於進一步緊縮貨幣政策的必要，有助於穩定美國公債殖利率，也削弱了美元的支撐力道。
AI類股本週大幅下跌，壓力也蔓延至部分信用市場。由於投資人已大量押注AI供應鏈各個環節，如今開始擔心資料中心營運商可能無法及時實現獲利，進而償還債務。
StoneX全球市場研究主管Matt Weller表示，「我認為今天乃至本週最值得關注的現象，是美元與AI交易之間的緊密連動。通常科技股遭到拋售時，市場會預期美元因避險需求而走強。我們確實看到部分資金流向債券，但美元實際上卻在下跌。」
本週英鎊與瑞士法郎兌美元的升幅居前。瑞士法郎受到避險需求支撐，市場也預期，即使利率環境進一步走低，瑞士仍不太可能將政策利率降至目前零利率以下。
英鎊兌美元上漲0.31%，至1英鎊兌1.3314美元，本週累計上漲0.63%。
美元兌瑞士法郎則下跌0.25%，至0.8246瑞郎，本週累計下跌0.67%。瑞郎在過去兩個交易日累計升值逾1.4%。
芝商所（CME）FedWatch工具顯示，市場預估聯準會本月稍晚維持利率不變的機率為83%，高於一個月前的49%。
聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)週五出席在曼谷舉行的國際貨幣基金（IMF）與世界銀行年度會議時，並未透露未來利率決策的線索。他表示，自己不會「預先判斷」任何一次會議的決策。
紐約梅隆銀行宏觀經濟策略師John Velis表示，「我認為，目前聯準會決策委員會內部，尤其是理事們，尚未形成足夠共識支持10月升息。不過，12月是否升息仍是未解之題，從現在到那時還有許多事情可能發生。」
歐元區財政風險仍受關注
法國財政風險仍是市場關注的背景因素。10月初，法國債務風險溢價曾大幅攀升。
歐元兌美元上漲0.08%，至1歐元兌1.1227美元。歐元週四已上漲0.56%，創下兩個月來最大單日漲幅，全週上漲約0.23%。
投資人預期，美國總統川普將避免讓中東或烏克蘭局勢進一步升級，因為更大規模的衝突可能推升通膨，進而損害他在期中選舉前的政治支持度。
美元兌日元下跌0.08%，至158.11日元。日元終止連續四週貶值走勢，本週升值0.13%。此前，伊朗衝突支撐美元走強。
近期油價上漲推升美元，同時對歐元與日元等能源進口國貨幣造成壓力。
日本銀行（BOJ）總裁植田和男(Kazuo Ueda)週五再次強調，潛在通膨率可能超越央行設定的2%目標，仍是需要留意的風險。

paras_en: The dollar fell on Friday (the 16th), with both the euro and the yen posting their first weekly depreciation in more than a month, reflecting a cooling of market expectations for further Fed rate hikes and lingering investor worries that AI is weighing on equity markets.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, slipped 0.17% to 101.87, down about 0.35% for the week.

Consumer price and producer price data released this week came in above expectations, briefly unsettling markets. However, comments from Fed officials indicated no urgent need for further monetary tightening, helping to stabilise US Treasury yields and weakening support for the dollar.

AI‑related stocks fell sharply this week, and the pressure spread to parts of the credit market. Investors, who have heavily bet on every link of the AI supply chain, are now worried that data‑center operators may not generate profits quickly enough to service their debt.

Matt Weller, head of global market research at StoneX, said, "I think the most noteworthy phenomenon today and this week is the tight link between the dollar and AI trading. Usually when tech stocks are sold off, the market expects the dollar to strengthen on safe‑haven demand. We did see some flows into bonds, but the dollar actually fell."

The pound and the Swiss franc posted the biggest gains against the dollar this week. The franc was supported by safe‑haven demand, and markets expect that even if rates fall further, Switzerland is unlikely to push its policy rate below the current zero‑percent level.
The pound rose 0.31% to $1.3314, up 0.63% for the week.
The dollar slipped 0.25% against the Swiss franc to 0.8246 CHF, down 0.67% for the week. The franc had appreciated more than 1.4% over the past two trading days.
CME’s FedWatch tool shows the market now assigns an 83% probability that the Fed will keep rates unchanged later this month, up from 49% a month ago.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh attended the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday and offered no clues about future rate decisions, saying he does not "pre‑judge" the outcome of any meeting.

John Velis, macro strategy strategist at BNY Mellon, said, "I think the Fed’s policy committee, especially the governors, have not yet reached sufficient consensus to support a rate hike in October. However, whether there will be a hike in December remains an open question, and many things could happen between now and then."
Euro‑area fiscal risks remain a focus.
Fiscal risk in France continues to be a background concern for markets, with French sovereign risk premiums spiking sharply in early October.
The euro rose 0.08% to $1.1227. It had gained 0.56% on Thursday, the biggest single‑day rise in two months, and is up about 0.23% for the week.

Investors expect that President Trump will try to avoid further escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine, as a larger conflict could push inflation higher and damage his political support ahead of the mid‑term elections.
The dollar fell 0.08% to ¥158.11, ending a four‑week streak of depreciation for the yen, which rose 0.13% this week. Previously, the Iran conflict had supported a stronger dollar.
Recent oil price gains have lifted the dollar while putting pressure on currencies of energy‑importing countries such as the euro and yen.
Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated on Friday that a potential inflation rate above the BOJ’s 2% target remains a risk to watch.

items.title: 〈台幣〉股匯不同調 續貶7.3分失守32.3元關卡
items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Weakens While Stocks Hold, Falling 0.73 ¢ to Slip Below the 32.3 TWD Mark
paras: 在美元指數維持強勢、外資持續撤出亞洲市場影響下，新台幣兌美元今 (16) 日走弱，終場收在32.338元，貶值7.3分，續創近期波段低點，顯示國際資金仍偏向美元資產，相較於昨天的91億美元爆巨量，台北外匯經紀公司與元太外匯經紀公司合計總成交量為 46.12億美元。
儘管匯市承壓，台股表現相對有撐，加權指數終場收在47,111點，上漲141點，漲幅約0.3%，呈現匯弱股強格局。市場買盤主要聚焦 AI 伺服器、高階 PCB 及半導體供應鏈族群，在電子權值股支撐下，大盤成功守住漲勢。
從籌碼面來看，統計今日三大法人合計賣超約729億元，其中外資賣超高達494億元，已連續第8個交易日站在賣方；投信則持續扮演護盤角色，買超約132億元，寫下連6買；自營商賣超約367億元。
市場人士指出，本波新台幣轉弱主要受到美元升值效應帶動，近期美國經濟數據維持韌性，加上市場重新評估聯準會後續政策路徑，推升美元買盤，亞洲主要貨幣同步承壓，新台幣也不例外。資料顯示，10月以來新台幣已由31字頭一路走貶至32.3元以上水準。
觀察資金流向，外資近期持續調節台股權值股與電子類股部位，成為匯市與股市的重要變數。不過投信買盤明顯進場承接，加上AI相關產業基本面未見轉弱，因此支撐台股維持高檔震盪格局。今天市場呈現「匯率偏空、股市偏多」，除外資匯出導致台幣走弱，加上AI、高效能運算(HPC)及先進封裝需求仍強，吸引國內資金與長線買盤進駐，使台股維持相對強勢。
paras_en: Under a strong US dollar index and continued foreign‑capital outflows from Asian markets, the New Taiwan dollar weakened against the US dollar today (Oct 16), closing at 32.338 TWD, down 0.73 ¢ and extending its recent low‑point swing, indicating that international funds remain biased toward dollar assets. In contrast to yesterday’s massive USD 91 billion turnover, Taipei’s foreign‑exchange brokers and Yuan‑Tai FX brokers together handled a total volume of USD 46.12 billion.

Despite pressure on the currency market, Taiwan’s equity market showed relative resilience, with the weighted index closing at 47,111 points, up 141 points or about 0.3%, reflecting a “weak currency, strong stocks” pattern. Buying interest centered on AI servers, high‑end PCBs and semiconductor supply‑chain groups, and the rally in heavyweight electronics stocks helped the market maintain its upward momentum.

From a flow perspective, the three major institutional investors sold a combined net NT$729 billion today, with foreign investors leading the sell‑side at NT$494 billion for the eighth consecutive trading day. Trust funds continued to play a stabilising role, net‑buying about NT$132 billion for the sixth straight session, while proprietary traders sold roughly NT$367 billion.

Market observers said the recent weakening of the Taiwan dollar is mainly driven by the dollar’s appreciation. Recent US economic data remain resilient and the market’s reassessment of the Fed’s policy path has boosted dollar demand, putting pressure on major Asian currencies, including the TWD. Data show that since October the Taiwan dollar has slid from the low‑31s to above the 32.3 TWD level.

Looking at capital flows, foreign investors have been adjusting their positions in Taiwan’s heavyweight and electronics stocks, becoming a key variable for both the FX and equity markets. However, trust‑fund buying is evident, and the fundamentals of AI‑related industries have not weakened, supporting the Taiwan stock market’s high‑level range‑bound pattern. Today’s market displayed a “bearish currency, bullish equity” stance: foreign outflows weakened the TWD, while strong demand for AI, high‑performance computing and advanced packaging kept domestic and long‑term buying interest in equities, allowing the stock market to stay relatively strong.

隨著人工智能(AI)公司債務沉重的憂慮，推動資金湧入美國公債避險，拖累美元兌日圓至157.53低點，但美國當周初請失業金人數增至19.9萬低於預期及9月零售銷售較前月增0.8%超過預估值，並據數據顯示紐約聯邦儲備銀行10月製造業指數升至25.5，而且美國9月最終需求生產者物價指數(PPI)分別較前月與去年同期漲1.3%及6.3%，創四年半最大漲幅，限制美元走低。預估今日美元兌日圓阻力於158.10-30，支撐於157.10-30。
◆EUR/USD
昨日澳洲公布9月失業率維持五年高位4.7%，就業人口則較前月減少3.93萬人，降幅為去年2月以來最大，8月就業人數亦下修至2.93萬人，促使澳洲央行(RBA)在11月及12月升息的機率分別跌至約9%及28%，打擊澳幣下挫，而且國際貨幣基金(IMF)警告能源衝擊與收益率上升，或拖累亞洲明年經濟增長放緩，拖累歐元兌美元觸及1.1147低點。
據歐元區公布8月工業生產分別較前月與上年同期跌0.5%及1.1%，而且歐洲央行(ECB)管理委員會委員佩雷拉認為歐元區能元通貨膨脹未見蔓延，但法國9月消費者物價調和指數(HICP)較去年同期漲3.4%，創2024年1月以來最高，而且美元走軟，提振歐元兌美元至1.1240高點。預估今日歐元兌美元支撐於1.1170-90，阻力於1.1260-80。
◆GBP/USD

週四英國央行(BOE)首席經濟學家皮爾認為投資人不應將BOE未來一次升息解讀為一系列的開端，但英國8月國內生產總值(GDP)意外較前月增長0.1%及較去年同期成長2.1%為近四年最強，而且製造業產出與工業生產分別較前月增1.2%及0.8%較佳，激勵英鎊兌美元自1.3181低點上漲。據BOE副總裁布里登稱，英國企業自行消化能源衝擊有助控制通貨膨脹，而且英國財政大臣希利本月提交預算案將增強經濟韌性及恪守財政紀律，推升英鎊兌美元至1.3277高點。預估今日英鎊兌美元支撐於1.3240-60，阻力於1.3340-60。

Houthi forces and Iran have intensified attacks on Saudi Arabia and vessels transiting the Hormuz Strait, sending gasoline prices soaring and accelerating the U.S. September consumer price increase. At the same time, the Federal Reserve’s Beige Book shows rising fuel costs adding price pressure, which could further damage President Trump and the Republican Party ahead of the November 3 election. Fed officials have also issued cautious remarks, pushing the benchmark 10‑year Treasury yield down to a three‑week low and reducing market bets on an October rate hike, which kept the dollar subdued on Thursday. In addition, Japan’s August core machinery orders rose 5.2% month‑over‑month and 18.6% year‑over‑year, beating expectations. BOJ policy‑board member Junko Koeda said inflation carries a sizable upside risk and the Bank should not be overly cautious on rate hikes, noting that Japan’s neutral rate is well above 1%, indicating room for further policy‑rate increases. Finance Minister Shunichi Suzuki also declared that Japan has left deflation behind, will balance growth with fiscal discipline, support the yen, and as the Japanese stock market plunged, funds fled to Japanese government bonds for safety, while exporters and speculators sold, pulling the USD/JPY down from its 158.33 peak.

With concerns over heavy debt loads at AI companies prompting a flight to U.S. Treasuries, the dollar fell to a 157.53 low against the yen. However, initial jobless claims rose to 199,000, below expectations, and September retail sales increased 0.8% month‑over‑month, beating forecasts. The New York Fed’s October manufacturing index rose to 25.5, and September’s final demand PPI jumped 1.3% month‑over‑month and 6.3% year‑over‑year—the biggest rise in four‑and‑a‑half years—supporting the dollar. The dollar/yen resistance is projected at 158.10‑30 with support at 157.10‑30 today.
EUR/USD

Yesterday Australia reported a September unemployment rate of 4.7%, the highest in five years, while employment fell by 39,300, the biggest monthly decline since February 2022. August employment was also revised down to 29,300. This pushed the probability of RBA rate hikes in November and December to about 9% and 28% respectively, weighing on the Aussie dollar. The IMF warned that energy shocks and rising yields could slow Asian growth next year, dragging the euro down to a low of 1.1147 against the dollar.

Euro‑zone August industrial production fell 0.5% month‑over‑month and 1.1% year‑over‑year. ECB Governing Council member Pierre Wunsch said inflation has not yet spread across the euro area, but France’s September HICP rose 3.4% year‑over‑year, the highest since January 2024. A weaker dollar lifted the euro to a 1.1240 high. The euro/dollar support is estimated at 1.1170‑90 with resistance at 1.1260‑80 today.
GBP/USD

On Thursday BOE chief economist Huw Pill warned investors not to read a single future rate hike as the start of a series. Yet Britain’s August GDP unexpectedly rose 0.1% month‑over‑month and 2.1% year‑over‑year, the strongest in four years, while manufacturing output and industrial production grew 1.2% and 0.8% respectively, boosting the pound from a low of 1.3181. BOE deputy governor Ben Broadbent said UK firms’ self‑mitigation of energy shocks helps contain inflation, and Finance Minister Jeremy Hunt’s budget this month aims to strengthen economic resilience and fiscal discipline, lifting the pound to a 1.3277 high. The pound/dollar support is projected at 1.3240‑60 with resistance at 1.3340‑60 today.

items.title_en: <New York Forex> Dollar Falls, Bond Rally Eases Inflation Data Impact
paras: 美元周四(15日)自18個月高點回落，投資人將目光從強勁的美國通膨與消費支出數據，轉向 AI 資料中心業者債券遭拋售的情況。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌 0.45%，報 101.99。此前美國通膨數據高於預期，美元指數週三升至 18 個月高點。
美國 9 月生產者物價(PPI)以 4 年半來最快速度上漲，商品與服務成本同步增加，進一步顯示通膨壓力正從能源領域擴散至其他領域。
上個月零售銷售增幅高於預期，主要受到汽油價格上漲帶動，每週初領失業救濟金人數則小幅增加，顯示消費需求仍具韌性，勞動市場也維持穩定。
但美國公債價格上漲，美元則回落，反映聯準會(Fed)官員近期發表審慎言論，進一步降低市場對 10 月升息的預期。
Monex USA交易主管 Juan Perez 表示，「目前市場存在一種不利美元的論述，原因在於，通膨若維持在這樣的水準，且以如此快的速度上升，將難以持續。」
他表示，「無論戰事方面沒有好消息，或股市前景看起來悲觀，在過去四週美元大幅走強之後，市場仍傾向拋售美元……經濟停滯似乎對交易員的想法產生更大的影響。」
AI企業債務負擔受關注
美元回落帶動歐元反彈，歐元兌美元上漲 0.56%，從 18 個月低點升至 1.1218 美元，創下近兩個月來最大單日漲幅。
英鎊兌美元則上漲 0.64%，至 1.3275 美元，此前數據顯示，英國經濟 8 月意外成長 0.1%。
週三美國消費者物價指數（CPI）數據高於預期，最初推升市場對聯準會維持高利率更長時間的押注。同時，市場再度擔憂 AI 企業沉重的債務負擔，促使資金流向美國公債等避險資產，市場走勢因而震盪加劇。
Mesirow Currency Management 資深投資策略師 Uto Shinohara 表示，「晶片股遭拋售為債券提供支撐，使殖利率得以維持在相對受控的水準，抵銷通膨訊號帶來的影響。」
芝商所（CME Group）FedWatch 工具顯示，交易員目前預期，聯準會在 10 月 27 日至 28 日的會議上維持利率不變的機率為 73%，高於一個月前的 53%。
CPI 報告公布後，市場對升息的預期機率大幅上升，但聯準會負責監管事務的副主席鮑曼 (Michelle Bowman)，以及舊金山聯準銀行總裁戴莉 (Mary Daly) 等官員表示，聯準會可以等到會議前取得更明確的資訊再做決定，隨後市場對升息的押注便有所降溫。
LMAX Group 市場策略師 Joel Kruger 表示，「如果殖利率難以進一步走高，而美元每逢反彈便持續遭到賣出，將會強化我們的看法：通膨消息大致已被市場消化，風險的整體平衡將有利於風險性資產。」
投資人週五也將關注聯準會官員在曼谷舉行的國際貨幣基金（IMF）與世界銀行年度會議上的談話，包括聯準會主席華許 (Kevin Warsh)，以尋找美國央行下一步行動的線索。
澳幣兌美元下跌 0.77%，至 0.6919 美元，此前澳洲 9 月就業人數意外減少。
日元則升值 0.15%，至每美元兌 158.08 日元。
Shinohara 表示，「聯準會即將進入政策會議前的靜默期，而會議前也不再有一級重要經濟數據公布，因此市場走勢可能仍將受到俄羅斯與烏克蘭、伊朗相關地緣政治不確定性，以及 AI 產業發展的影響。」

paras_en: The dollar fell on Thursday (the 15th) from an 18‑month high as investors shifted their focus from strong U.S. inflation and consumer spending data to the sell‑off in bonds of AI data‑center operators.

In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, slipped 0.45% to 101.99. Earlier, U.S. inflation data came in above expectations, pushing the index to an 18‑month peak on Wednesday.

U.S. September producer prices (PPI) rose at the fastest pace in four and a half years, with costs for goods and services climbing together, further showing inflation pressure spreading from the energy sector to other areas.

Last month’s retail sales growth exceeded expectations, driven mainly by higher gasoline prices, while initial unemployment claims rose slightly, indicating consumer demand remains resilient and the labor market stays stable.
However, U.S. Treasury prices rose and the dollar retreated, reflecting recent cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials that further lowered market expectations of a rate hike in October.

Juan Perez, head of trading at Monex USA, said, "There is currently a narrative that is unfavorable to the dollar because if inflation stays at this level and rises this quickly, it will be hard to sustain."

He added, "Whether there is no good news on the war front or the equity outlook looks bleak, after the dollar’s strong run over the past four weeks the market still tends to sell the greenback… stagnation seems to have a bigger impact on traders’ thinking."
AI companies' debt burdens draw attention
The dollar’s decline lifted the euro, which rose 0.56% against the dollar from an 18‑month low to $1.1218, marking the biggest single‑day gain in nearly two months.
The pound rose 0.64% to $1.3275 after data showed the U.K. economy unexpectedly grew 0.1% in August.

Wednesday’s U.S. consumer price index (CPI) came in above expectations, initially boosting bets that the Fed would keep rates high for longer. At the same time, renewed worries about heavy debt loads at AI firms prompted a flow into safe‑haven assets such as U.S. Treasuries, intensifying market volatility.

Uto Shinohara, senior investment strategist at Mesirow Currency Management, said, "The sell‑off in chip stocks provided support for bonds, keeping yields at relatively controlled levels and offsetting the impact of inflation signals."
The CME Group FedWatch tool shows traders now assign a 73% probability that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its Oct. 27‑28 meeting, up from 53% a month ago.

After the CPI report, the market’s probability of a rate hike surged, but Fed Vice‑Chair Michelle Bowman and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said the Fed could wait for clearer information before deciding, cooling the market’s rate‑hike bets.

LMAX Group market strategist Joel Kruger said, "If yields struggle to rise further and the dollar keeps getting sold each time it rebounds, it reinforces our view that inflation news has largely been priced in and the overall risk balance will favor risky assets."
Investors will also watch Friday for comments from Fed officials at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, including Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, for clues on the central bank’s next move.
The Australian dollar fell 0.77% to $0.6919 after September job numbers in Australia unexpectedly dropped.
The yen appreciated 0.15% to 158.08 per dollar.

Shinohara noted, "The Fed is entering a pre‑meeting quiet period, and no major economic data will be released before the meeting, so market moves may still be influenced by geopolitical uncertainties related to Russia, Ukraine, Iran, and the development of the AI industry."

items.title: 〈台幣〉股匯雙殺再現！匯市爆91億美元巨量 重摔近2角收32.265元
items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Faces Dual Stock‑Currency Slump Again! FX Market Swells to $9.115 Billion, Drops Nearly 2 ¢ to 32.265
paras: 台北外匯市場今(15)日上演股匯雙殺戲碼，在外資大舉撤出、台股重挫逾千點衝擊下，新台幣兌美元匯率終場收在32.265元，重貶1.92角，成交金額更放大至 91.15 億美元，顯示市場避險情緒急遽升溫。今日外資及陸資單日淨賣超逾3000億元，成新台幣重貶的最大主因。
新台幣今日以32.11元開出後一路走弱，盤中最低來到32.452元，最低一度崩跌 3.79 角，終場收32.265元，改寫逾 2 個月新低。台北及元太外匯市場總成交量爆出 91.15 億美元的天量，直接打破歷史單日最高成交量紀錄。
匯銀人士指出，今日新台幣走勢主要受到外資大規模匯出影響，而背後關鍵則來自台股出現恐慌性賣壓。市場憂心全球科技股修正及資金風險偏好下降，導致外資同步在股市與匯市進行調節。
觀察今日台股表現，加權指數終場收在46969.87點，大跌1655.96點，跌幅達3.41%，成交值約新台幣1.43兆元，市場氣氛急速轉弱。
法人動向更顯示資金撤離力道驚人。根據證交所統計，三大法人今日合計賣超3700.76億元，其中外資及陸資賣超3025.55億元，自營商賣超958.24億元，僅投信逆勢買超283.03億元。進一步觀察，外資及陸資今日賣出金額高達6773.6億元，遠高於買進的3748.05億元，單日淨賣超逾3000億元，成為新台幣重貶的重要推手。
市場人士分析，近期美元續獲避險資金青睞，加上美債殖利率維持高檔，使亞洲貨幣普遍承壓。加上台股面臨外資調節電子權值股壓力，連帶新台幣跌勢較區域貨幣更加明顯。且今日匯市成交量明顯放大至逾91億美元，遠高於一般交易日水準，反映出口商、進口商及外資同步進場調節部位。
從技術面觀察，新台幣近期持續在32元整數關卡附近震盪，今日收盤已回落至32.265元，代表市場短線仍以美元需求為主。若後續外資持續匯出，不排除匯價仍有測試32.3元至32.5元區間的可能。
今日股匯市同步大幅震盪，也凸顯國際資金流向已成為牽動台灣金融市場的關鍵因素，後續外資是否止血，將成為觀察新台幣能否穩住32元關卡的重要指標。
paras_en: Taipei’s foreign‑exchange market staged a double‑whammy of stocks and currency today (15th), as foreign investors pulled out en masse and the Taiwan stock index plunged over a thousand points. The New Taiwan dollar closed at 32.265 per US dollar, a depreciation of 1.92 ¢, with transaction volume ballooning to $9.115 billion, indicating a sharp rise in market hedging sentiment. Foreign and mainland Chinese investors posted a net sell‑off of more than NT$300 billion for the day, the main driver of the dollar’s steep fall.

The New Taiwan dollar opened at 32.11 and weakened throughout the session, hitting a low of 32.452, a drop of 3.79 ¢ at its deepest point, and closed at 32.265, breaking a more‑than‑two‑month low. The Taipei and Yuan‑Tai foreign‑exchange markets together recorded a record‑high daily turnover of $9.115 billion, shattering the previous single‑day volume record.

Currency‑bank officials said the dollar’s move was mainly driven by massive foreign‑exchange outflows from overseas investors, with the underlying cause being panic selling in the Taiwan stock market. The market fears a correction in global tech stocks and a decline in risk appetite, prompting foreign investors to adjust positions in both equities and FX simultaneously.

Looking at today’s stock performance, the weighted index closed at 46,969.87 points, down 1,655.96 points or 3.41%, with a turnover of about NT$1.43 trillion, reflecting a rapid weakening of market sentiment.

Institutional flows further highlight the magnitude of capital outflows. According to exchange statistics, the three major institutional groups sold a combined NT$370.076 billion today, with foreign and mainland Chinese investors net‑selling NT$302.555 billion and proprietary traders selling NT$95.824 billion, while only investment trusts bought a net NT$28.303 billion. More specifically, foreign and mainland Chinese investors sold NT$677.36 billion versus purchases of NT$374.805 billion, a net daily sell‑off of over NT$300 billion, becoming a key force behind the dollar’s sharp depreciation.

Market analysts note that the US dollar continues to attract safe‑haven flows, and US Treasury yields remain high, putting pressure on Asian currencies. Coupled with foreign investors trimming exposure to Taiwan’s heavy‑weight electronic stocks, the New Taiwan dollar has weakened more than regional peers. Today’s FX turnover surged past $9.1 billion, far above normal trading‑day levels, reflecting exporters, importers and foreign investors all adjusting positions together.

From a technical perspective, the New Taiwan dollar has been oscillating around the 32.00 mark. Today’s close at 32.265 suggests short‑term market demand remains dollar‑driven. If foreign outflows persist, further testing of the 32.30‑32.50 range cannot be ruled out.

The simultaneous large swings in stocks and FX today underscore that international capital flows have become a pivotal driver of Taiwan’s financial markets. Whether foreign investors can halt the outflow will be a key gauge for the dollar’s ability to hold the 32.00 level going forward.

items.title: 瑞銀維持美元「逢低買進」策略
items.title_en: UBS Maintains "Buy the Dip" Strategy for the Dollar
paras: 《Investing.com》報導，瑞銀(UBS)週三(14日)在給客戶的報告中表示，只要能源價格維持高檔，且AI投資題材持續發酵，逢美元回檔時買進仍是合適的策略。
策略師Shahab Jalinoos表示，G10貨幣市場本週走勢相對平淡，法國與德國10年期公債殖利率利差穩定在約140個基點。
他指出，從法國的角度來看，這個利差水準仍令人不安，也持續支持歐元兌美元應採取「逢高賣出」策略的觀點。
瑞銀預期，歐元將測試第四季的區間低點1.1050，並維持2026年底目標價1.1200不變。
Jalinoos指出，柴油價格可能接近穩定的初步跡象，為歐元提供部分支撐。然而，歐洲仍面臨風險，天然氣庫存處於異常低檔，天然氣期貨價格也升至本輪週期新高。
近期科技股走勢疲軟，可能促使美元進入部分整理階段，通膨數據也可能進一步降低市場對未來較長期間升息的預期。
他寫道，「儘管如此，我們的核心觀點仍未改變：只要能源價格維持高檔，且AI帶動的投資題材持續發酵，逢美元走低時買進仍是合適的策略。」
在商品貨幣方面，瑞銀認為，澳幣、紐幣與加幣目前處於整理階段，但由於市場對升息的定價有限，這三種貨幣都有機會收復9月的跌幅。其中，加幣是瑞銀最偏好的短線做多標的。
Jalinoos也反駁了「日本減持法國債券將推升日元」的看法。他表示，國際收支數據顯示，日本對法國債券的曝險部位已大幅下降。
paras_en: Investing.com reported that UBS on Wednesday (the 14th) said in a client report that as long as energy prices stay high and AI‑related investment themes keep developing, buying the dollar on dips remains an appropriate strategy.
Strategist Shahab Jalinoos noted that G10 currency markets were relatively flat this week, with the spread between French and German 10‑year government bond yields steady at about 140 basis points.
He pointed out that from a French perspective this spread level is still unsettling and continues to support the view that the euro versus the dollar should be sold on rallies.
UBS expects the euro to test the fourth‑quarter low of 1.1050 and keeps its year‑end‑2026 target unchanged at 1.1200.

Jalinoos said diesel prices may be showing early signs of stabilisation, offering some support to the euro. However, Europe still faces risks as natural‑gas inventories are at unusually low levels and gas futures have risen to a new high for this cycle.
Weakness in recent tech stocks could push the dollar into a partial correction, and inflation data may further reduce market expectations for prolonged rate hikes.

He wrote, "Nevertheless, our core view remains unchanged: as long as energy prices stay high and AI‑driven investment themes continue to develop, buying the dollar on its declines remains an appropriate strategy."

Regarding commodity currencies, UBS sees the Australian, New Zealand and Canadian dollars as currently in a consolidation phase, but with limited rate‑hike pricing in the market each has a chance to recover September losses. The Canadian dollar is UBS’s top short‑term long‑biased pick.

Jalinoos also rebutted the view that Japan’s reduction of French bond holdings would boost the yen, noting that balance‑of‑payments data show Japan’s exposure to French bonds has already fallen sharply.
